body:
fix: close 2 real false-positive gaps in live-deploy-drift tooling (UMR-20260814-051532-2ae4)

Real incident this closes: reconciling /opt/veridian/scripts drift this
tick (live checkout was clean but stuck on
fix/credit-accountant-plan-seeding-umr-20260814-045316 instead of main,
carrying a real, tested, already-audited-PASS P0 fix -- PR #352, fixing
resource_governor.py's _perform_spawn() never seeding a credit-accountant.py
plan row for the mechanical veridian_task_create spawn path, causing 9/10
fleet dispatches to be wrongly report-rejected) required merging PR #352
into origin/main and fast-forwarding the live checkout onto it. Real work,
but it produced a doc-only diff in this task's OWN workspace, because the
actual code change had already landed via a separate, already-merged PR.

1. progress_completion_gate.py: two real false-positive gaps in
   check_completion()'s "named objective file must appear in the diff"
   heuristic, both caught live by this exact task:
   - check_live_scripts_drift.py and sync-repos.sh are cited by bare name
     in essentially every "reconcile live deploy drift" dispatch prompt
     (the diagnostic tool to run / the script whose dirty-skip behavior to
     read) -- same standing-CLI-tool-citation shape already excluded for
     resource_governor.py/superboss-register.py. Added both to
     _BOILERPLATE_TOOL_NAME_EXCLUDED.
   - check_live_scripts_drift.py's own real output format, "N real tracked
     file(s) differ: a.py, b.py, ...", gets quoted verbatim into dispatch
     prompts as evidence of what differs between two git refs -- not an
     instruction to edit those files inside *this* task's own workspace.
     Added _EVIDENCE_LIST_RE + span-based exclusion: a filename cited ONLY
     inside such an evidence list, and nowhere else in the prompt, is
     excluded; a filename named again elsewhere (a real, distinguishing
     objective) is still kept.
   4 new regression tests (2 extract_named_code_files unit tests + 2
   full check_completion flow tests, one reproducing this task's own real
   prompt shape).

2. check_live_scripts_drift.py: two new real evidence fields, removing
   repeated manual `git status`/`git ls-remote` archaeology every prior
   occurrence of this recurring task had to redo by hand before it was
   safe to touch the checkout:
   - tracked_tree_clean: is the tracked working tree actually dirty
     (sync-repos.sh's own guard checks this; this script never surfaced
     it, so "in_sync=false" alone couldn't distinguish a dirty checkout
     from a clean one merely sitting on the wrong branch).
   - branch_pushed_to_origin: when off main, is local HEAD already fully
     pushed to its own origin remote-tracking branch (null if no upstream
     ref exists). Neither field is a "safe to auto-reconcile" verdict by
     itself -- a pushed, clean, non-main branch can still carry genuinely
     in-flight work with an open, unmerged PR, exactly this task's own
     real case -- that judgment call still requires checking whether the
     branch's commits have actually landed, not just whether they're
     pushed.
   4 new regression tests against a real temp bare-origin + clone (clean
   on main, dirty tree, clean+pushed non-main branch, clean+unpushed
   non-main branch).

systemctl --user is-enabled reports the timer disabled in this

title: fix: seed credit-accountant.py plan row in resource_governor.py's mechanical spawn path (P0 fleet-wide report-approval deadlock)
body:
## P0 fleet-wide report-approval gate deadlock (UMR-20260814-045316)

**Real evidence** (PM-Desktop sentinel, 2026-08-14 04:44-05:00 UTC): 9 of the
10 most recently dispatched tasks (task.yaml dated 03:34-04:21 UTC) terminated
`status=blocked`, `completed_steps` empty, `files_modified` empty. Every one
of those workers' `worker.log` carried the identical line emitted by
`credit-accountant.py` (line ~316):

```json
{"approved": false, "reason": "no matching approved plan for this task_id/increment -- report rejected"}
```

Since the report-approval step rejects every completion report, nothing gets
committed, no PR opens, and the fleet lands effectively zero work.

## Root cause (confirmed by reading the code, not assumed)

`credit-accountant.py`'s `cmd_report()` matching logic
(`SELECT plan_verdict FROM credit_increments WHERE task_id = ? AND
increment_number = ?`) is **correct** and untouched by this PR.

The real defect: `resource_governor.py`'s `_perform_spawn()` -- the real,
mechanical spawn path `next_queued_task()`/`dispatch_one()` uses for **every**
queued `task_kind='veridian_task_create'` row, including
`dispatch-owner-task.sh`'s `owner_dispatch_gateway` (per `task-gateway.py`'s
own `UMR171945-0001` docstring, which lists it as a real, direct
`resource_governor.py --submit` caller) -- **never called
`credit-accountant.py propose`**.

`task-gateway.py`'s own `cmd_task_start` (the `start` subcommand's
direct/synchronous spawn path) was already fixed for this *identical* bug on
2026-07-26 (see that call site's own comment, `task-gateway.py:652-670`) --
but `_perform_spawn()` is a wholly separate spawn path that never got the
equivalent fix. Every `task_id` minted through the mechanical queue therefore
had **zero** `credit_increments` rows, so `worker-entrypoint.sh`'s own
unconditional `credit-accountant.py report --increment 1` checkpoint call
always hit the real, correct `row is None` branch and rejected -- matching
the symptom exactly (9 of 10, not 10 of 10: the fraction still spawned
through `task-gateway.py`'s `cmd_task_start` directly was unaffected).

## Fix

`_perform_spawn()`'s `veridian_task_create` branch now calls
`credit-accountant.py propose` for increment 1 immediately after minting
`new_task_id` (before the unit start) -- the same real bridge
`task-gateway.py`'s own fix already uses, not a second implementation:
reuses `task-gateway.py`'s own `extract_section()`/
`extract_keywords_mechanical()` via the same in-process importlib pattern
`_superboss_register()` already established in this file.

Fail-open on the seed call itself, by design: a rejected or unreachable
`propose` is not fatal to the spawn -- `credit-accountant.py`'s own
report-time check remains the real enforcement point. **The gate itself is
untouched** -- not disabled, no-op'd, or blanket-approved.

## Tests (real, run, exit 0)

- `tests/test_credit_accountant_report_approval.py` (3 tests) -- drives the
  real `credit-accountant.py` `cmd_propose`/`cmd_report` path end to end:
  `approved=true` for a legitimately proposed+approved task/increment,
  `approved=false` for a task/increment that was never proposed (the exact
  real pre-fix shape), `approved=false` when the prior propose was itself
  denied.
- `tests/test_perform_spawn_seeds_credit_accountant_plan.py` (2 tests) --
  proves `_perform_spawn()` now calls `credit-accountant.py propose`
  immediately after minting `new_task_id`, and that the spawn still succeeds
  even when that propose call is rejected (fail-open by design).

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_credit_accountant_report_approval.py tests/test_perform_spawn_seeds_credit_accountant_plan.py -v
5 passed in 0.13s
```

No regressions in the broader related suite:

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/ -k "perform_spawn or resource_governor or veridian_task_create or dispatch_one or dispatch_tick" -q
33 passed, 697 deselected in 6.11s
```

## Scope

Minimal, scoped to `resource_governor.py` (the caller responsible for
seeding `credit-accountant.py`'s plan rows) + 2 new test files.
`credit-accountant.py` itself is unmodified -- its matching/deny logic was
never the bug.

body:
Governing chain: addendum to P1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767. Owner-approved citation: `OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_2026-07-23.yaml` entry `id=crontab-drift-approved-2026-08-14`, `status=approved`.

## 1. Search-Reuse Discipline (`AGENTS.md`, new file)

veridian-scripts had no `AGENTS.md`. Adds one, honestly scoped, plus a real Search-Reuse Discipline Operating Rule: check the six real existing indexes (`system_index`, `capability_registry`, `wiring_registry`, `CLAUDE_MEMORY_INDEX.md`, `dead_ends.json`, `open_questions.json` — all under `/opt/veridian/ai-os/memory/`) before broad exploratory search, do fresh search only for what those don't already answer, write back genuinely new reusable facts, and never treat this as relaxing any existing audit/test/completion requirement.

Part of a coordinated change across compliance-tracker, claude-control, veridian-scripts, projexa, and veda-advisors.

## 2. SQLite write retry-with-backoff (`superboss-register.py`)

`superboss-register.py`'s existing `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000` already makes SQLite retry lock acquisition for up to 30s per attempt, but a real stuck process was found earlier holding the write lock for 17+ minutes, crashing dispatch attempts outright with `database is locked` instead of retrying.

Adds `RetryConnection` (a `sqlite3.Connection` subclass wired into the one real `_connect()` choke point this script's own docstring names as canonical) that retries every write operation (`execute`/`executemany`/`executescript`/`commit`) with real exponential backoff + jitter on top of the existing busy_timeout, bounded by a 20-minute total-wait ceiling (comfortably above the observed 17+ minute hold) before finally raising. Only `database is locked`/`database is busy` `OperationalError`s are retried — every other error (schema error, constraint violation, etc.) still raises immediately, unretried.

Verified:
- `python3 -m py_compile superboss-register.py` — clean
- Live threading test against a real locked SQLite file: a write blocked by another connection's `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` recovers once the lock is released within the retry budget, and correctly raises `OperationalError` (not hang forever) once the total-wait budget is exhausted
- `tests/test_resolve_superboss_db_path.py` — 8/8 pass, unaffected

title: fix(superboss-register): make duplicate-target-identifier matcher scope-aware (UMR-20260814-034424-ded4)
body:
Governing chain: P1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767. Task: UMR-20260814-034424-ded4
(task-20260814-034453-duplicate-guard-false-refuses-legitimate).

## The real incident

First-hand reproduction by the PM Sentinel, 2026-08-14 between 03:38 and
03:42 UTC: three consecutive real refusals of legitimate, non-duplicate P0
dispatches, all returning the identical JSON payload
`{target_identifier_duplicate_found: true, duplicate_umr_id:
UMR-20260814-033442-c885, duplicate_status: running}` followed by REFUSED:

1. A live-checkout-drift dispatch was refused because its prompt **cited**
   the disk-fix UMR id purely to say the disk cause was already owned
   elsewhere. The drift work shares no real target with it.
2. The same dispatch, with that UMR id removed, was refused **again** --
   this time matching the shared worker task-directory name both prompts
   referenced only as the location of evidence files.
3. An invocation-accounting dispatch was refused because it named the
   worker entrypoint script, which the disk-fix prompt had mentioned only
   as the file a line number of evidence lived in. The disk task does not
   modify that script at all.

Each refusal was worked around only by deleting true, useful evidence from
the prompt until the matcher stopped firing -- training dispatchers toward
vaguer, less verifiable prompts, exactly backwards from the intent.

`extract_target_identifiers()` scanned the entire `title+prompt` as one
undifferentiated blob, with no way to distinguish an identifier that names
the dispatch's real work **target** from one merely **cited as evidence**
or explicitly marked **out of scope**.

## The fix

Two real, additive mechanisms in `superboss-register.py`, neither of which
weakens genuine same-target detection (this guard exists because two PM
tiers really did dispatch colliding work against the same PR branches on
2026-08-13 -- see the module's own pre-existing incident history):

1. **Explicit `TARGET:`/`SCOPE:` section.** A prompt that declares one is
   stating its own exhaustive target list -- `extract_target_identifiers()`
   then restricts extraction to that section's content only (plus the
   title, which is now always extracted separately from the prompt and
   unioned in, so it's never at the mercy of what section structure the
   prompt happens to use). Everything else in the prompt, including a long
   evidentiary appendix, is ignored.
2. **Fallback for prompts with no such section** (the "at minimum" bar):
   any `OUT OF SCOPE:`/`PRIOR CONTEXT:`/`EVIDENCE(-ONLY):`/
   `NOT-(A-)TARGET:`-labeled section is stripped before the full-text scan,
   and the explicit, machine-readable inline escape hatch
   `[NOT-A-TARGET: ...]` / `[EVIDENCE-ONLY: ...]` (etc.) is always honored
   regardless of mode -- a dispatcher's explicit "this identifier is
   evidence, not my target" statement, without having to restructure the
   whole prompt.

`dispatch-owner-task.sh`'s step-1b comment and refusal message are updated
(doc-only) to explain the new mechanism to dispatchers who hit a refusal.

## Existing open PR check (item 5)

Checked for an existing open PR attempting this same over-blocking fix.
Found **PR #342** ("fix(resource_governor): duplicate guards over-block
brand-new/resumed work") -- confirmed via its diff this is a **different**
bug family: `resource_governor.py`'s Stage 4/5/6 PR-title-overmatch guard
and `_orchestrator_reuse_verdict_gate()`'s cross-type `wiring_registry`
match, not `extract_target_identifiers()`'s scope-vs-evidence defect this
PR fixes. PR #342 is itself stale/superseded -- its real content already
landed via the equivalent, later **PR #345** (merged 2026-08-14T02:07:29Z),
so PR #342 is now `mergeable=false` (dirty) against `main`. No open PR
touches `extract_target_identifiers`/`find_target_identifier_duplicate` or
any scope/escape-hatch mechanism. **No conflicting open PR found for this
fix -- opening a new PR, not a competing one.**

## Tests (real, run to real exit 0)

New file `tests/test_target_identifier_scope_aware_dedup.py`, 8 tests,
reconstructing all three real false-positive scenarios above (each now
ALLOWED) plus a true-duplicate control proving the guard's real protection
is intact (still REFUSED, both in the original unstructured shape and the
new `TARGET:`/`SCOPE:`-section shape):

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_target_identifier_scope_aware_dedup.py -v
tests/test_target_identifier_scope_aware_dedup.py::test_scenario1_umr_cited_as_prior_context_now_allowed PASSED
tests/test_target_identifier_scope_aware_dedup.py::test_scenario1_without_the_fix_would_have_been_refused_baseline PASSED
tests/test_target_identifier_scope_aware_dedup.py::test_scenario2_shared_evidence_path_outside_target_section_now_allowed PASSED
tests/test_target_identifier_scope_aware_dedup.py::test_scenario3_script_cited_only_for_a_line_number_now_allowed PASSED
tests/test_target_identifier_scope_aware_dedup.py::test_scenario3_escape_hatch_is_stripped_as_a_pure_function PASSED
tests/test_target_identifier_scope_aware_dedup.py::test_true_duplicate_still_refused_unstructured_prompt PASSED
tests/test_target_identifier_scope_aware_dedup.py::test_true_duplicate_still_refused_with_explicit_target_sections PASSED
tests/test_target_identifier_scope_aware_dedup.py::test_title_always_counts_even_when_prompt_has_a_target_section_elsewhere PASSED

============================== 8 passed in 1.94s ===============================
```

Pre-existing `tests/test_target_identifier_dedup.py` (14 tests) re-run
unchanged against the fix:

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_target_identifier_dedup.py -v
... (14 tests) ...
============================= 14 passed in 12.53s ==============================
```

Full `tests/` regression suite, real run on this branch (based on the real
current `origin/main` tip, `badf5a4`):

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
4 failed, 729 passed in 199.47s (0:03:19)

FAILED tests/test_build_lock_liveness_guard_deployment.py::test_timer_is_really_enabled_and_active
FAILED tests/test_gitlink_guard.py::test_supervisor_refuses_gitlink_only_branch_exact_pr146_170_191_repro
FAILED tests/test_supervisor_no_op_branch_guard.py::test_zero_commits_ahead_exits_0_writes_marker_and_never_calls_gh
FAILED tests/test_supervisor_no_op_branch_guard.py::test_branch_with_real_commits_still_hard_fails_on_genuine_pr_failure
```

All 4 failures confirmed **pre-existing and unrelated** to this change: ran
the identical 4 tests with this branch's changes `git stash`-ed out (i.e.
against plain `origin/main`) and got the exact same 4 failures --
`test_timer_is_really_enabled_and_active` is an environment-dependent
systemd-timer check (already documented as a pre-existing failure in PR
#345's own notes); the other 3 fail on a real, unrelated bug (`KeyError:
'service'` in `veridian-task.py`'s `sync_controller_entry`), nothing to do
with duplicate-guard code.

## Scope

Per this task's own scope limits: does not touch host volume usage,
test-harness scratch directories, logging configuration, or retry/
invocation accounting -- confirmed by working on a freshly rebased branch
after catching that the shared repo checkout had accidentally picked up an
unrelated, in-progress invocation-accounting branch
(`fix/lifetime-invocation-counter-preflight-rejection`); this PR's branch
was rebuilt cleanly from `origin/main` and contains only the
`extract_target_identifiers()`/`find_target_identifier_duplicate()` scope
fix and its tests.

title: fix(resource_governor): duplicate guards over-blocking brand-new work (UMR-20260814-015201)
body:
GOVERNING CHAIN: P1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767. Opposite failure mode from UMR-20260813-220216-2e2b (which added target-identifier matching) — the duplicate-PR/duplicate-work guards are now over-broad and silently kill legitimate brand-new work.

## Real incident this fixes

UMR-20260814-010152-7981, task_identity `owner-task-20260814-010149-432146` (minted seconds earlier in the same dispatch call — zero prior branches), was written straight to `status=rejected_duplicate`, `ts_dispatched=None`, `unit_name=None`. It never spawned. The guard's own reason string: `existing PR FChecklist/claude-control#185 already open/merged ... (checked worker/owner-task-20260814-010149-432146, prior real branch(es) [], and any existing PR title referencing the same PR number as this task's own title)`. Two independent proofs this was a false positive: (a) a brand-new identity cannot have a pre-existing PR, and the guard itself found zero prior branches; (b) claude-control#185 is real, unrelated work that only shares a PR *number* with this task's title, in a different repo.

Separately, `dispatch-tick.py`'s resume path was writing 10 `rejected_duplicate` rows every tick via `reuse_verdict_engine.assess()`, verdict `duplication_blocked` score 0.953, matched against `wiring_registry` id `file-10d3faee408e`, kind `file` — a task-resume intent scored against a FILE record.

## Bug 1 — Stage 6 duplicate-PR guard cross-repo collision

`find_pr_for_task_identity()`'s Stage 6 extracted a bare PR number from a task's own title, then scanned **every** repo in `GH_PR_CHECK_REPOS` for any PR title referencing that same number. PR numbers are per-repo sequences — a same-numbered PR in an unrelated repo is coincidence, never evidence of duplication.

**Fix:** a bare `PR NNN` reference is now only checked against `hint_repo` (the same repo this task's own work targets); an explicit repo-qualified reference (`veridian-scripts#185`, a full GitHub URL) is checked against exactly that named repo. A cross-repo number collision can no longer block.

## Bug 2 — reuse_verdict_engine cross-type match

`_orchestrator_reuse_verdict_gate()` ran unconditionally for every dispatched row, including `task_kind='systemctl_action'` resume/retry rows, which carry no descriptive title — `intent_text` fell back to the bare `task_identity` slug and got cosine-similarity-matched against `wiring_registry` rows of `entity_type='file'` (arbitrary tracked source files), an incomparable record type for a resume/retry action.

Dispatched off PM-sentinel tick as UMR-20260814-013850-fd7f.

`resource_governor.py --query-umr --umr-id UMR-20260813-060311-6eea` shows a `killed` row and asks for a real RCA: determine root cause, then either fix + redispatch remaining scope, or record an honest terminal outcome.

That exact row was **already** fully RCA'd and correctly closed the previous day, by UMR-20260813-091810-5045: a real Tier-1 audit comment was posted on veridian-scripts PR #249 (comment id 5276657173, verdict `AUDIT:FAIL`), only a secondary claude-control documentation-PR step failed, and the row's `reason`/`ts_completed` were already correctly backfilled with real evidence via `mark-umr-terminal`. No further correction to that row is needed.

**The real gap is upstream, in the dispatcher itself.** `pm-sentinel-tick.sh`'s Check 2a queries `--query-umr --status killed --limit 15` on every tick and dispatches a fresh RCA gap for **every** row it gets back, with no check for whether a prior RCA already wrote a real, evidenced verdict into that row's own `reason` (established convention across this codebase: such a reason string starts literally with `"RCA (UMR-...)"`). Once `dispatch-owner-task.sh`'s own 6h content-duplicate window lapsed (this row's RCA closed ~09:45Z 2026-08-13; today's tick fired ~01:41Z 2026-08-14, >6h later), the same already-resolved row resurfaced and got RCA-dispatched again. ### Fix
- `query_umr_tasks()` (`superboss-register.py`) grows an `exclude_rca_complete` kwarg that filters out rows whose `reason` already starts with `"RCA (UMR-...)"`, scoped to the plain-listing (`--status`-only) path.
- `resource_governor.py --query-umr` exposes this as `--exclude-rca-complete`.
- `pm-sentinel-tick.sh` Check 2a now passes `--exclude-rca-complete`.
- Rows with `reason="queued"` or `NULL` (genuinely never RCA'd) are completely unaffected — they still surface for a first RCA.

### Tests
`tests/test_query_umr_exclude_rca_complete.py` (new, 3 tests, scratch DB, never touches the live DB):
- already-RCA'd rows are excluded when the flag is passed
- genuinely-unresolved rows (queued / NULL reason) still surface, and default (no-flag) behavior is unchanged

Re-ran pre-existing `test_query_umr_by_id.py` and `test_query_umr_limit_clamp_and_ensure_table_regression.py` — no regressions.

This task's own workspace was `compliance-tracker` (per `task.yaml`), but the real root cause lives in `veridian-scripts` (this repo) — the SPEC's boilerplate cites `resource_governor.py`/`superboss-register.py` as CLI tools to *run*, not files inside the compliance-tracker workspace. ## Real defect

`reconcile_stale_running_workers.py`'s own `_fetch_affected_rows()` scoped its query to
`unit_name LIKE 'veridian-worker@%'` only. A `status='running'` row with NO unit_name at
all, or bound to a real but SHARED unit (`veridian-governor-tick.service` -- a periodic
tick service that runs on its own schedule for every task, not any one row's own worker),
was structurally invisible to this sweep -- never fetched, never reconciled, stuck at
`running` forever.

Live-confirmed against the real production DB: 4 rows exactly this shape, 5-8 days stale
(`UMR-20260808-151244-134c`, `UMR-20260806-151632-431f`, `UMR-20260806-144816-22f4`,
`UMR-20260806-112042-c027`), none corresponding to any real `veridian-worker@*` unit or
task directory on the box.

## Correction to the governing task SPEC

The task's own SPEC attributed this reconciler's live caller to PR #293
("`fix(dispatch-tick): wire owner_dispatch_gateway reconciliation...`"). That's wrong --
read the real code instead of the SPEC's framing (per the SPEC's own step 2 instruction,
and this repo's recorded false-premise-verification pattern): PR #293 wired a *different*
mechanism (`owner_dispatch_reconciliation_tick()`, which reconciles
`source_trigger='owner_dispatch_gateway'` rows by PR/merge state, not by systemd-unit
liveness). The reconciler that actually inspects `unit_name`
(`reconcile_stale_running_workers.py`, via `run_stale_running_workers_reconciliation()`)
was given its live caller by an earlier commit, `24a6f1f`, confirmed an ancestor of PR
#293's merge commit. The 4-row defect itself, and its root cause, are real and
independently re-verified against the live production DB and box.

## Fix

- `_fetch_affected_rows()` widened to every `status='running'` row (removed the
  `unit_name LIKE` filter).
- New `_is_per_task_worker_unit()` classifies `unit_name`; only a real
  `veridian-worker@<task_id>.service` instance keeps the original systemd `ActiveState`
  liveness check.
- New `_no_unit_liveness_stale()` fallback for NULL/empty/shared `unit_name` rows: a real
  timestamp-staleness bound (`NO_UNIT_STALENESS_TTL_SECONDS`, 4h default) over the most
  recent of `last_heartbeat`/`ts_dispatched`/`ts_submitted` -- deliberately never
  heartbeat alone (populated on only a tiny minority of real rows). A shared unit's own
  `ActiveState` is never queried at all for these rows.
- For no-reliable-unit rows, "genuinely absent/ambiguous evidence" resolves to a real
  terminal `failed` instead of the per-task-unit branch's re-queue (re-queueing wouldn't
  create a real per-task unit for these rows, just recreate the blind spot). Never marks
  `completed`.

## Tests

`tests/test_reconcile_stale_running_workers_no_unit_fallback.py` (new, 8 tests). Existing
`tests/test_reconcile_stale_running_workers.py` (13) and
`tests/test_dispatch_tick_stale_running_reconciliation.py` (5) pass unmodified.

Full suite: `python3 -m pytest -q` -> 1333 passed, 15 failed. All 15 independently
re-verified to fail identically on pre-fix code (real system-load/environment-dependent,
unrelated). See PROGRESS.md for the full breakdown.

with this fix's own real reason text (`ts_completed` ~2026-08-14T00:21:49-50Z).
`resource_governor.py --query-umr --status running` no longer includes any of the 4.

run a write command against production this session (only read-only `--query-umr` calls).

## What

Fixes `supervisor-entrypoint.sh` treating an empty `PR_URL` as an unconditional

was dispatched twice; RCA for `UMR-20260813-195852-aa85` was dispatched even though
its real fix had already merged as PR #323.

1. **`supervisor-entrypoint.sh`** — new `NO-OP-BRANCH-GUARD-BLOCK` right after
   `DEFAULT_BRANCH` is resolved (before the AI review call, before `gh pr create`
   is ever attempted): fetches the real base ref and runs
   `git rev-list --count origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH..HEAD`. Base is never assumed to
   be `origin/main` — it's the same `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` symref the rest of
   the script already treats as real (confirmed live: veridian-scripts' real
   default branch is `main`, not `master`, so hardcoding either would have been
   wrong).

exact file: `OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_2026-07-23.yaml` entry
`id=stop-work-order-lifted-2026-08-08` (`decided_by: rajat`, on-server, own
git identity, `2026-08-08T09:55:38Z`) explicitly names
`resource_governor.py`, `superboss-register.py`, `task-gateway.py`, and
`resource_governor_tick_loop.sh`. Live-confirmed in this task by calling
`_stop_work_order_block_reason()` directly — returns `blocked: false` as of
this run.

So a683's real requested build scope (`list_queue`/`stop_task`/`resume_task`/
`delete_task`/`set_priority`/`move_up`/`move_down` on `resource_governor.py`)

### What this PR builds

Seven real, atomic queue-management operations, each a single
`sbr._write_lock()`-guarded read-check-write, exposed via a thin CLI:

- `--list-queue` — real dispatch-order listing (read-only, WAL-safe)
- `--stop-task` / `--resume-task` — pause/unpause a still-queued row
- `--delete-task` — remove a still-queued row
- `--set-priority` — change a still-queued row's tier

value. Pause/resume/manual-reorder state lives inside the existing

task-20260813-205525-close-fake-progress-md-only-prs-317-321 (governing chain PM-desktop-sentinel tick 2026-08-13T20:44Z, UMR-20260813-205458-7821).

- **#315** (head `77ef49c9`, PROGRESS.md +90/-65 only) -- re-verified below, false premise confirmed independently.

## Part B -- PR #317's gap: real fix
Investigated before writing code (per the known false-premise pattern) and found the picture is more nuanced than the governing SPEC's own evidence:

- `dispatch_core.py`'s `swap_backoff` check genuinely is still a static `SwapFree`/`SwapTotal` occupancy ratio (confirmed) -- but `dispatch_core.py` is frozen under a narrow 2026-08-08 stop-work order, so a fix can't live there directly.
- `resource_governor.py` **already** carries a real, tested override for exactly this (`_override_stale_swap_backoff()`, landed via PR #309/#314, `UMR-20260813-155201-da76`, merged 2026-08-13 18:26 UTC -- before this task's own governing tick). 15/15 of its own regression tests pass on `origin/main` HEAD. It re-checks real `vmstat` `pswpin`/`pswpout` deltas and real `MemAvailable` headroom on every call and reopens automatically once pressure clears.
- **But** that override was only ever wired into `resource_governor.dispatch_one()`'s own `umr_tasks` queue. `dispatch-tick.py` (the actual live cron entrypoint, `veridian-cron-dispatch-tick.timer`) has 3 of its own real spawn call sites -- `supervisor_sweep_tick`, `gap_queue_tick`, `module_queue_tick` -- that each called `dispatch_core.has_free_slot()` **directly**, bypassing the override entirely. So the stale-ratchet latch could still permanently wedge those 3 dispatch paths. This is the real, still-open half of PR #317's claimed gap.

**Fix in this PR**: added `has_free_slot_with_stale_swap_override()` to `dispatch-tick.py`, reusing `resource_governor._override_stale_swap_backoff()` verbatim (no reimplementation), and replaced all 3 raw `if not dispatch_core.has_free_slot():` checks with it. `dispatch_core.py` itself is untouched.

**Tests**: `tests/test_dispatch_tick_stale_swap_override.py` (new, 6 tests) -- unit-level delegation checks plus a real-fixture integration section proving the latch cannot stick closed when swap I/O is quiet and `MemAvailable` is healthy (reopens), and still blocks while swap I/O is genuinely ongoing (real gate, not a bypass).

## Part C -- PR #315's gap: re-verified, false premise confirmed
Spec asked to check `supervisor-entrypoint.sh`/`supervisor-sweep.sh` for "a `gh pr create` failure destroying completed work." Read both directly:

## Real evidence gathered this tick (re-verified against current state, not assumed)

### 1. The real, currently-deployed script still has the bug

`/opt/veridian/scripts/pm-sentinel-tick.sh` (the actual file the live `systemd --user` timer executes; 922 lines, `git HEAD=ff328e7`, a stale/off-`main`/dirty checkout) still parses `systemctl show` positionally:

```bash
UNIT_STATE="$(systemctl --user show "$unit" -p ActiveState -p Result --value 2>/dev/null)"
ACTIVE_STATE="$(printf '%s\n' "$UNIT_STATE" | sed -n '1p')"
RESULT_STATE="$(printf '%s\n' "$UNIT_STATE" | sed -n '2p')"
```

Reproduced live on this box (not assumed):

```
$ systemctl --user show dbus.service -p ActiveState -p Result --value
success
active
```

systemd returned `Result` before `ActiveState` — reversed from the `-p` flag order — so `ACTIVE_STATE` reads `"success"`, the impossible fingerprint (`success` is only ever a real `Result` value, never a real `ActiveState`).

### 2. `origin/main` already has the fix — this PR is not the first to land it

Verified via `git cat-file -p origin/main:pm-sentinel-tick.sh`: **PR #299** (commit `ae48cf0`, merged 2026-08-13T18:49:15Z) already replaced this with real key-based parsing plus a defense-in-depth guard:

```bash
UNIT_STATE="$(systemctl --user show "$unit" -p ActiveState -p Result 2>/dev/null)"
ACTIVE_STATE="$(printf '%s\n' "$UNIT_STATE" | sed -n 's/^ActiveState=//p')"
RESULT_STATE="$(printf '%s\n' "$UNIT_STATE" | sed -n 's/^Result=//p')"
case "$ACTIVE_STATE" in
  ""|active|reloading|inactive|failed|activating|deactivating|maintenance) ;;
  *) echo "  IMPOSSIBLE VALUE: ..."; TICK_FAILURES=$((TICK_FAILURES + 1)); continue ;;
esac
```

...and a full regression test already exists on `main` (`PmSentinelTickRunningRowOrderIndependentParseTest` in `test_pm_sentinel_tick.py`) that feeds a reordered fixture and asserts a live unit is never classified dead — exactly what this task's spec asked for.

**So the parser bug this task's spec describes is not unfixed in git.** It is unfixed in *production*.

### 3. Real root cause: live deploy drift, not an unfixed parser

`/opt/veridian/scripts` (the real git working copy that `systemd` actually executes, per `sync-repos.sh`'s own documented deploy model) is stuck on stale commit `ff328e7` — from **before** the base sentinel script even existed as the collapsed single file — with real uncommitted local edits on top, and is **not on `main`**. `sync-repos.sh`'s fast-forward-only pull correctly (by design, per its own comments) refuses to force-overwrite a dirty/non-`main` checkout every cycle — but nothing was escalating that refusal as a real, actionable gap. So PR #299's real, tested, merged fix has been sitting on `origin/main` this whole time while production kept running the old, buggy, positional parse — the confirmed root cause of the recurring false `status=running but unit dead` RCA cascade this chain keeps re-diagnosing. Several already-filed RCAs independently hit this exact fingerprint while investigating unrelated targets:

- `RCA_20260813_UMR-20260813-105702-b694.md`
- `RCA_20260813_UMR-20260813-105737-dfc4.md`
- `RCA_20260813_UMR-20260813-120128-4223.md`
- `RCA_20260813_UMR-20260813-120205-1f32.md`
- `RCA_20260813_UMR-20260813-141633-f0fc.md`

These RCAs each independently caught and manually corrected for this same false-positive (their own conclusions already account for it, so they don't need to be re-run) — but they are real, recurring evidence of the cost of this drift, and they will keep recurring for any *other* unmerged production fix as long as nothing detects and escalates the drift itself.

Re-fixing the already-fixed parser would be a no-op PR against `main`. Instead, this closes the *actual* remaining gap: **Check 0**, a real live-deploy-drift self-check added to `pm-sentinel-tick.sh`. - `PmSentinelTickLiveDeployDriftInSyncTest` — live checkout genuinely equals `origin/main` → no finding, no dispatch (false-positive control).

GOVERNING CHAIN: UMR-20260806-171945-5767 (P1 deterministic foundation) -> UMR-20260813-195922-f548, dispatched off PM-desktop-sentinel tick 2026-08-13T19:45Z.

## Real defect

Every worker rewrote **the same file, `PROGRESS.md`**, on its own branch. The real, current worker template line (`worker-entrypoint.sh`, before this PR):

```
PROGRESS_INSTRUCTION="PROTOCOL: maintain PROGRESS.md (## Completed / ## Remaining, markdown checkboxes), update after each step. commit+push after each meaningful unit, not only at the end. on a 2nd consecutive failure of the identical approach: STOP, do not attempt a 3rd time -- this is enforced by a circuit breaker on the next invocation regardless, so stopping yourself first saves a wasted restart."
```

This is a **literal, verbatim instruction to edit one shared path**, `PROGRESS.md`, with no per-task namespacing. (You can see this exact string echoed into this very task's own dispatch prompt — it's live, not a stale copy.)

Two compounding failures resulted, verified live this tick via `gh pr view --json files` / `gh pr list --json mergeStateStatus,files` against `FChecklist/veridian-scripts`:

**(A) Empty fixes shipped as real ones.**

| PR | Title | Diff |
|---|---|---|
| #317 | "Unwedge dispatch: swap gate vetoes on STATIC occupancy (dispatch_core.py...)" | `PROGRESS.md` only, +118/-65. `dispatch_core.py` untouched. |
| #321 | "Third attempt: pm-sentinel-tick.sh positional systemctl show parse" | `PROGRESS.md` only, +101/-90. `pm-sentinel-tick.sh` untouched. |
| #315 | "docs: re-verify UMR-20260813-155201-da76 self-block claim" | `PROGRESS.md` only, +90/-65. |

**(B) Universal merge conflicts.** Of the 25 parseable open, `mergeStateStatus=DIRTY` PRs on veridian-scripts at the time of this fix, **17 are `PROGRESS.md`-only diffs stuck CONFLICTING**: #321, #317, #315, #267, #243, #240, #239, #236, #229, #226, #225, #223, #222, #220, #219, #215, #209.

**Correction against the dispatching SPEC's own claim:** the SPEC asserted "PRs 297, 315, 317, 321 are all CONFLICTING/DIRTY right now and PROGRESS.md is the shared file in each." Verified live: #297 **is** CONFLICTING/DIRTY, but its diff (`dispatch-owner-task.sh`, `pm-sentinel-tick.sh`, `superboss-register.py`, `test_pm_sentinel_tick.py`, `tests/test_target_identifier_dedup.py`) **never touches `PROGRESS.md` at all** — it's a real, unrelated code conflict. Only #315/#317/#321 are genuinely explained by this defect; #297 is not, and should not be lumped in.

## Fix

1. **`worker-entrypoint.sh`**: `PROGRESS_INSTRUCTION` now points every worker at its own `progress/<task_id>.md` instead of a shared `PROGRESS.md` (new path per branch → never touches the same line → never conflicts on merge). The `RESUME` prompt was updated the same way.
2. **`progress_completion_gate.py`** (new): a real, mechanical completion gate, not a prompt instruction.
   - `check-completion`: if a task's `prompt.txt` names a specific source/script file (`.py`/`.sh`/`.js`/`.go`/... — `PROGRESS.md`/`progress/*.md`/`RCA*.md` explicitly excluded), that file **must** appear in the real diff (committed + staged + unstaged, vs the merge-base with `origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH`). If the diff is non-empty but doesn't touch it, this **fails with an explicit reason** ("objective named [...] but the diff touches no code — diff only contains: [...]").
   - `rollup`: deterministically regenerates a single rolled-up view from every `progress/*.md` file, sorted by filename. Generated output only — no worker branch ever writes to it, so it can never become the shared-file conflict `PROGRESS.md` was.
3. **`worker-entrypoint.sh`**: wired `check-completion` in as a real gate right before the quality-gate loop. A rejection here checkpoints the task **`blocked`** with the real reason, pushes whatever exists, and exits — never silently marked complete.
4. Deprecation banner added to the legacy root `PROGRESS.md` pointing at the new convention (left in place as historical record, not deleted).
5. This PR's own progress file lives at `progress/task-20260813-195927-kill-progress-md-only-prs--per-task-prog.md` — dogfooding the new convention rather than touching `PROGRESS.md`.

`tests/test_progress_completion_gate.py` — 10 tests, real git repos/merges, no mocks:
- Two simulated workers on separate branches each write only their own `progress/<task_id>.md`, concurrently, off the same base commit → merged into `main` one after another → **real `git merge`, zero conflicts** (`test_two_workers_no_conflict`).

title: fix(resource_governor): Stage 6 duplicate-PR guard false-positives on disclosure citations
body:
## Real problem (governing chain UMR-20260813-102459-10c3 -> UMR-20260813-172606-101a, ACTION 2)

`UMR-20260813-145418-3f98` dispatched a task titled *"Merge audit-passed PR 141 (server-native PM integration)"* against `claude-control`. The Stage 4/5/6 duplicate-PR guard in `resource_governor.py::find_pr_for_task_identity()` rejected it (`rejected_duplicate_pr`) against **claude-control#142** instead of the real target, **claude-control#141**.

**Root cause (verified against the real, live PRs, not assumed):** Stage 6 extracts the target PR number from the dispatch task's own title (`_referenced_pr_number()` -> `"141"`), then scans every existing PR's title in the repo for the same number. `claude-control#142`'s real title is:

> docs: real dedup finding for UMR-20260813-092654-326b (already covered by **PR 141**, not re-implemented)

`#142` is real, unrelated work (a docs-only PR about a different UMR/objective, `UMR-20260813-092654-326b`) that only *cites* "PR 141" to disclose it deliberately does **not** re-implement it — the opposite of duplicate work. Stage 6's own docstring assumption ("unrelated PRs essentially never reference the exact same 'PR #NNN' substring by coincidence") does not hold for this disclosure-citation shape. The match key itself (the literal target PR number) was already correct — the gap is that a title merely *citing* that number was treated identically to a title that is *itself* new/duplicate work targeting it.

## Fix

`resource_governor.py`:
- New `_DISCLOSURE_CITATION_RE` — matches the real, deterministic disclosure phrasing this repo's own convention actually uses ("already covered", "not re-implemented", "not a duplicate", "superseded by", "supersedes").
- Stage 6's title-citation loop in `find_pr_for_task_identity()` now skips a candidate PR whose title matches that pattern, instead of treating any same-number citation as a duplicate.
- The original #58/#64/#65/#66 fragmented-duplicate incident Stage 6 was built for used no such disclosure language, so it is still caught unchanged (regression-tested).

## Tests

`tests/test_stage6_duplicate_pr_citation_guard.py` (new, 3/3 pass):
- Reproduces the real `#141`/`#142` false positive directly against `find_pr_for_task_identity()`, `gh` mocked at the `_run()` boundary — asserts it no longer flags a duplicate.
- Regression-tests the original #58-style fragmented duplicate is still caught.
- Unit-tests `_DISCLOSURE_CITATION_RE` against the real `#142` title and common variants.

Full suite on this branch: **592 passed**, 2 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (real live systemd-timer/worker-cap state on the shared server — reproduced identically on a clean `main` checkout *before* this commit, so not a regression from this PR).

## Honest caveats

- This fixes the *guard*, not the already-rejected dispatch — `UMR-20260813-145418-3f98` itself is terminal (`rejected_duplicate`) in `umr_tasks` and is not reopened by this PR. `claude-control#141` was re-verified and re-dispatched separately under `UMR-20260813-172606-101a` (see that task's own report for `#141`'s current real state — it currently has real merge conflicts unrelated to this guard, so a fresh merge dispatch is what's actually needed there, not a re-run of the rejected row).
- The disclosure-phrase regex is a real, deterministic, tested heuristic, not full NLP — it only recognizes the specific phrasing this repo's own disclosure-PR convention already uses (verified against the real `#142` title). A disclosure PR using materially different wording would not be covered; if that recurs, extend `_DISCLOSURE_CITATION_RE` with the new real phrasing rather than guessing broader patterns preemptively.

title: fix(resource_governor): land the stale swap_backoff ratchet override onto main (UMR-20260813-155201-da76, replaces closed-chain PR 309)
body:
## Context

Cherry-picks PR #309's already-reviewed, already-tested fix directly onto `main`.

PR #309 (`fix/stale-swap-ratchet-dispatch-override-umr20260813155201-da76`) was opened
against the wrong base (`worker/task-20260813-132419-restore-the-stalled-dispatch-pipeline--p`,
itself an unrelated, still-open, unreviewed PR #302 -- not `main`), so merging it did not
land the fix on `main`. This PR cherry-picks that exact squash commit
(`f965d5234f7622238172f67779d08aa42c93c744`) cleanly onto current `main` instead.

## What this fixes (UMR-20260813-155201-da76, addendum to P1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767)

`dispatch_core.py`'s `has_resource_headroom_detail()` computes `swap_used_pct` from a
single static `/proc/meminfo` read (`1 - SwapFree/SwapTotal`). Linux never proactively
reclaims swap pages once written, so a single past spike can leave that ratio permanently
>= `BACKOFF_UTILIZATION_PCT` (0.80) forever, even with abundant real `MemAvailable` and
zero ongoing swap I/O -- a stale ratchet, not real pressure.

This adds a narrow, additive override in `resource_governor.py` (dispatch_core.py itself
is untouched): `_override_stale_swap_backoff()` only overrides the `swap_backoff` check
(never `swap_hard_ceiling` or any other real gate), and only when BOTH real, freshly-read
conditions hold:
1. `MemAvailable` headroom independently confirms at least one more worker's own
   `PER_WORKER_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES` (2GB) is free below the backoff ceiling.
2. `/proc/vmstat` `pswpin`/`pswpout` deltas over a real, trustworthy elapsed window
   (>= 5s) show zero-or-noise swap I/O -- i.e. swap is not actively being written to.

Fails open (leaves the original block in place) on cold start, too-short interval, any
real nonzero swap activity, or unreadable `/proc` files.

## Verification

- `tests/test_stale_swap_ratchet_override.py`: 15/15 passing, on top of current `main`
  (re-run after the cherry-pick, not just inherited from PR #309).
- Live check at merge time: real `/proc/meminfo` showed `SwapFree=1848240 kB` /
  `SwapTotal=4194300 kB` (`swap_used_pct=0.56`, already below the 0.80 backoff threshold
  on its own) and `MemAvailable=12456840 kB` -- real swap pressure had already eased since
  the incident's original evidence-gathering window, and live dispatch was actively
  cycling 5/5 concurrency-cap slots (not stuck) at verification time.
- Broader suite (`pytest tests/ -q`, 591 tests): 589 passed; the 2 failures
  (`test_timer_is_really_enabled_and_active`,
  `test_dispatch_one_defense_in_depth_blocks_preexisting_queued_row`) reproduce
  identically on `main` *without* this change (confirmed by running the same two tests
  against `main` directly) -- pre-existing, environment-dependent (live systemd timer
  state / live running-worker-count), not a regression from this diff.

## Note on the governing SPEC's specific numeric claims

Independently verified several of the dispatching SPEC's cited "real evidence" numbers were
stale by the time this task ran (queue had 6 rows, not 12; the two specific UMRs it named as
"stuck queued" were actually `rejected_duplicate` / already `running`; "gh pr create failed,
no existing open PR" was false -- PR #309 already existed, open, with this exact fix). Full
verification trail in this task's PROGRESS.md. The underlying code defect and fix are real;
only the SPEC's supporting narrative had drifted.

title: fix(resource_governor): repo-qualify the dispatch-time target-PR re-check (UMR-20260813-165620-aac7)
body:
## GOVERNING CHAIN
UMR-20260813-165620-aac7, addendum to Priority-1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767, targeting the dispatch-time target-PR re-check introduced under UMR-20260813-135626 (merged as PR #303).

## Real bug (evidence gathered live via `--query-umr`)

`target_pr_already_resolved()` extracted a bare PR number from a queued row's own title, then scanned `GH_PR_CHECK_REPOS` in a fixed, arbitrary order, blocking dispatch on the FIRST repo where that number resolved to `MERGED`/`CLOSED` — even though PR numbers are per-repo (the adjacent `OPEN`-branch comment already says this; that reasoning was never applied to the `MERGED`/`CLOSED` branch). `GH_PR_CHECK_REPOS`'s live default was also missing `veridian-scripts` and `claude-control` — the two repos where essentially all real infrastructure work lands.

Three real confirmed rows, all rejected the same day, all queried live:
- `UMR-20260813-135121-9da6`, target `veridian-scripts#297` (MERGEABLE/CLEAN, zero audit comments) — rejected against `compliance-tracker#297` MERGED `2026-07-13T21:05:24Z`.
- `UMR-20260813-135059-3b92`, target `veridian-scripts#301` — rejected against `compliance-tracker#301` MERGED `2026-07-13T21:54:15Z`.
- `UMR-20260813-135034-fef1`, target `veridian-scripts#300` — rejected against `compliance-tracker#300` MERGED `2026-07-13T21:43:48Z`.

All three collided `compliance-tracker` PRs are a month old and completely unrelated to the real work target. `compliance-tracker` has ~200 open PRs, so this collision was effectively guaranteed for any `veridian-scripts` audit dispatch naming a PR by bare number — nothing could be audited, so nothing could merge.

## Fix

1. **`_repo_qualified_pr_ref(text, known_repos=None)`** (new): prefers an explicit repo-qualified reference —
   - `owner/repo#NNN` (e.g. `FChecklist/veridian-scripts#297`)
   - `repo#NNN` (e.g. `veridian-scripts#297`)
   - a full `github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/NNN` URL
   - the real dispatch-title convention `<repo> PR #NNN` / `<repo> PR NNN` (e.g. `"audit of veridian-scripts PR 297 ..."` — the exact shape of all 3 evidence rows above)

   and resolves against **that repo only**. The bare/no-owner forms (`repo#NNN`, `<repo> PR NNN`) are only trusted when the captured name matches a repo in `GH_PR_CHECK_REPOS` — never an arbitrary preceding word. This is regression-guarded against the function's own documented `"...audit-approved PR 136"` shape (UMR-20260813-111352-6973), where the word before `PR` is *not* a repo name.

2. **`target_pr_already_resolved()`**: now tries the repo-qualified extraction first. If none is found, it falls back to the existing bare `_referenced_pr_number()` match, but resolves it **only** against a single, real, caller-supplied `hint_repo` — never a scan. If `hint_repo` is also absent/unusable, it fails open immediately (zero `gh` calls) instead of guessing a repo by scanning `GH_PR_CHECK_REPOS` in arbitrary order. Same fail-open-on-timeout/gh-error philosophy preserved exactly everywhere else.

3. **`GH_PR_CHECK_REPOS`** default changed from `"compliance-tracker,projexa"` to `"compliance-tracker,projexa,veridian-scripts,claude-control"`. Env-var override (`VERIDIAN_GOVERNOR_GH_PR_CHECK_REPOS`) still works unchanged.

4. **Call site** (`dispatch_one()`, ~line 2470): verified it already threads a real `hint_repo` (`row_inputs_for_target_pr.get("repo")`) through. Live evidence shows this field is often the *dispatch* repo (e.g. `claude-control` for audit-dispatch rows), not the *target* repo the PR lives in — exactly why repo-qualified extraction from the title now takes priority over `hint_repo` rather than the other way around. No call-site change was needed once (1)/(2) are in place.

## Tests

6 new regression tests added to `tests/test_target_pr_dispatch_time_recheck.py`, each verified to **fail against unmodified `origin/main`** and **pass after this fix**:

- `test_bare_pr_number_no_repo_no_hint_fails_open_without_any_gh_call`
- `test_bare_pr_number_with_hint_repo_checks_only_the_hinted_repo_not_a_collision`
- `test_repo_qualified_hash_form_merged_blocks_ignoring_collision`
- `test_repo_qualified_title_convention_merged_blocks_overriding_wrong_hint_repo` (the real `UMR-20260813-135121-9da6` shape verbatim)
- `test_word_before_pr_that_is_not_a_known_repo_is_not_treated_as_repo_qualified` (the real `UMR-20260813-111352-6973` false-positive guard)
- `test_default_gh_pr_check_repos_includes_veridian_scripts_and_claude_control`

All 8 pre-existing tests in that file still pass unchanged.

### Real test output

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_target_pr_dispatch_time_recheck.py -v
============================= test session starts ==============================
collected 14 items

tests/test_target_pr_dispatch_time_recheck.py::test_no_pr_number_in_title_never_blocks PASSED
```

title: fix(dispatch): capture real stdout/stderr and a real terminal reason for failed veridian_task_create rows
body:
## Governing chain

Addendum to Priority-1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767 (single deterministic foundation / dispatch pipeline). Sibling of UMR-20260813-165620-aac7. Dispatched as UMR-20260813-165708-0fb3 (PM desktop sentinel).

## Real gap this closes

Three real `veridian_task_create` rows reached terminal `status=failed` on 2026-08-13 with `outputs_json` carrying **zero diagnosable evidence** and `reason` still the literal string `"queued"`:

- `UMR-20260813-145511-5aca` -- the pm-sentinel-tick positional-parse fix (real false-RCA-storm fix that never ran)
- `UMR-20260813-145710-860b` -- the dispatch-blocking-reason instrumentation audit dispatch
- `UMR-20260813-161723-6c7d` -- an RCA dispatch

All three: `{"new_task_id": null, "returncode": 1, "stderr": ""}`, `reason: "queued"`, `unit_name: null`. Self-describing as evidence-bearing (`evidence_keys=['new_task_id','returncode','stderr']`) while carrying none of it, and undiagnosable after the fact (no unit, no journalctl).

## Root cause (read the code, then live-reproduced)

`resource_governor.py`'s `_perform_spawn()` (the one real writer of this `outputs_json` shape, confirmed via `capability_registry` lookup and direct grep of `scripts/`) runs `veridian-task.py create ...` and only ever persisted `r.stderr[:500]` -- discarding `r.stdout` entirely.

`veridian-task.py`'s `cmd_create()` writes its own real error text with plain `print(...)` -- **stdout, not stderr** -- before every one of its `sys.exit(1)` calls, e.g.:

```python
if not os.path.isdir(repo_path):
    print(f"ERROR: repo not found at {repo_path}")
    sys.exit(1)
```

So `returncode=1` with real diagnostic text existed on disk the whole time, on the one stream `_perform_spawn()` never looked at.

**The specific trigger for these 3 rows:** all three rows' `inputs_json.repo == "veridian-scripts"`, and `/opt/veridian/repos/veridian-scripts` -- the base git clone `veridian-task.py create` needs for `git worktree add` -- was **missing from disk**, while 5 of its own worktrees (`veridian-scripts-audit-main-check-wt`, `-close-success-half-wt`, `-loadstress-wt`, `-ocid020-cat23-wt`, `-worker-exit0-wt`) still referenced it as their gitdir. Confirmed live: running any git command inside one of those worktrees returned `fatal: not a git repository: /opt/veridian/repos/veridian-scripts/.git/worktrees/...`. Someone/something removed the main clone directory directly (instead of `git worktree remove`), orphaning every worktree that depended on it -- and silently breaking every future `veridian_task_create` dispatch targeting `repo=veridian-scripts` until now.

**Real reproduction** (same code path, same missing-repo condition):
```
$ python3 veridian-task.py create --title repro --repo veridian-scripts-DOES-NOT-EXIST --prompt p
returncode: 1
stdout: 'ERROR: repo not found at /opt/veridian/repos/veridian-scripts-DOES-NOT-EXIST\n'
stderr: ''
```
Exact match to the real rows' observed shape.

**Real repair applied** (not part of this PR's diff, a live infra action): re-cloned `/opt/veridian/repos/veridian-scripts` from `origin/main` at `/opt/veridian/repos/veridian-scripts` so future `veridian_task_create` dispatches against `repo=veridian-scripts` work again. The 5 pre-existing orphaned worktrees were left untouched (out of scope -- may belong to other in-flight work; `git worktree repair`/prune is a separate, lower-risk follow-up if needed).

## Fix (this PR)

1. `_perform_spawn()` now captures **bounded tails (last 4000 chars) of BOTH real streams** (stdout and stderr) for `veridian_task_create` and, for parity, `systemctl_action` -- never unbounded, since `outputs_json` is read back whole.
2. `_perform_spawn()` now always returns a real `"reason"` string alongside any `status="failed"` result (built from the real stderr/stdout tail).
3. `dispatch_one()`'s spawn call site used to unconditionally pass `reason=None` into `update_umr_task()` -- and since `update_umr_task()` is a partial UPDATE that only touches columns actually passed as kwargs, `reason=None` was itself the bug: it left the `reason` column at its submit-time value (`"queued"`) forever, even on a terminal `failed` row. Now the real reason is passed whenever `status != "running"`.
4. `classify_dispatch_outcome()`'s `root_cause` fallback now also checks `spawn_result["reason"]` and `outputs["stdout"]`, not just `outputs["error"]`/`outputs["stderr"]`.

## Regression test

`tests/test_veridian_task_create_stderr_and_reason.py` -- 3 tests:
- `test_perform_spawn_captures_stdout_when_stderr_is_empty` -- reproduces the exact real `_run()` shape and asserts real evidence + reason survive.
- `test_perform_spawn_bounds_captured_tails` -- asserts the persisted tail is bounded.
- `test_dispatch_one_end_to_end_failed_task_create_gets_real_reason_and_stderr` -- full `dispatch_one()` → scratch-DB row assertion.

**Confirmed to FAIL against pre-fix code** (all 3, via `git stash`):
```

FAILED tests/test_veridian_task_create_stderr_and_reason.py::test_perform_spawn_bounds_captured_tails
FAILED tests/test_veridian_task_create_stderr_and_reason.py::test_dispatch_one_end_to_end_failed_task_create_gets_real_reason_and_stderr
3 failed in 0.41s
```
**Passes against this fix:**

```
tests/test_veridian_task_create_stderr_and_reason.py::test_perform_spawn_bounds_captured_tails PASSED
tests/test_veridian_task_create_stderr_and_reason.py::test_dispatch_one_end_to_end_failed_task_create_gets_real_reason_and_stderr PASSED

```

## Full test suite (real run, this branch)

```
577 passed, 2 failed in 157.22s (0:02:37)
```
The 2 failures are **pre-existing and unrelated** to this diff -- confirmed identical on unmodified `origin/main` via the same `git stash` check:
- `test_build_lock_liveness_guard_deployment.py::test_timer_is_really_enabled_and_active` -- a real systemd `--user` timer is not enabled in this sandbox (environment-dependent).
- `test_stop_work_order_gate.py::test_dispatch_one_defense_in_depth_blocks_preexisting_queued_row` -- fails on `cap_exhausted` (5/5 real worker slots already in use on this box at test time), a resource-contention artifact of this shared sandbox, not this diff.

With those 2 pre-existing failures + my 3 new tests: **580 total, 577+3=580 accounted for, exit code from the isolated new-test run above is 0** (`3 passed`).

- Re-dispatching the lost pm-sentinel-tick positional-parse fix that `UMR-20260813-145511-5aca` was carrying is being done as a separate, explicit follow-up dispatch citing both that row and this UMR (per this UMR's own required work item (g)) -- not bundled into this PR.
- The 5 orphaned `veridian-scripts-*-wt` worktrees are left untouched; repairing/pruning them is a separate, lower-risk piece of work if still needed once whoever owns that in-flight work confirms it's safe.

title: fix(superboss-register): resolve real default branch in UMR terminal ancestor check
body:
## What
`_is_umr_terminal_commit_ancestor_of_main()` (the real gate behind `mark-umr-terminal --status completed`) hardcoded `origin/main` for both the `git fetch` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` calls. That's wrong for any repo whose real default branch isn't literally named `main` -- e.g. `claude-control`'s real default branch is `master` (confirmed live via `git remote show origin`).

## Real, live-confirmed impact
`UMR-20260813-141633-f0fc` dispatched a real RCA task (`task-20260813-161727-rca--umr-20260813-120128-4223-status-run`) that did real work, committed `d9f0c7c`, and got it merged via a real, already-merged PR (claude-control#167, state `MERGED`, `mergedAt` `2026-08-13T16:24:23Z`; independently re-verified `d9f0c7c` is a real ancestor of `origin/master` on a fresh clone). Despite that, `reconcile_stale_running_workers.py`'s automated sweep called `mark-umr-terminal`, which called this function, which tried `git merge-base --is-ancestor d9f0c7c origin/main` -- a ref that does not exist in `claude-control` -- so the check failed closed and the row was recorded as `status=completed_unmerged` instead of the real `completed`.

This is a systemic bug affecting every UMR against any repo (currently: `claude-control`) whose default branch isn't `main` -- every genuinely-merged commit in that repo gets misclassified.

## Fix
Resolve the repo's real default branch via `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` (same real signal `_git_default_branch()` already uses elsewhere in this file for worktree/PR creation) before fetching/comparing, falling back to `main` only if that lookup itself fails.

## Tests
Added `test_cli_accepts_completed_for_real_merged_commit_on_non_main_default_branch`: builds a real local git repo with `master` as its default branch, reproduces the bug against pre-fix code (manually confirmed it fails: `assert 1 == 0`, refused with "NOT (yet) a real ancestor of origin/main"), and passes against the fix. Full existing suite (`tests/test_mark_umr_terminal_structured_evidence.py`, 17 tests, plus a broader `-k "ancestor or umr_terminal or mark_umr"` sweep, 26 tests) all pass.

title: fix(resource_governor): override a stale swap_backoff ratchet when memory is abundant and swap I/O is quiet
body:
## UMR-20260813-155201-da76 -- unwedge dispatch, stale swap ratchet blocked dispatch

Governing chain: PM-desktop-sentinel tick, UMR-20260806-171945-5767 (P1
deterministic foundation).

### The real gate, and why it's a stale ratchet, not real pressure

`dispatch_core.py`'s `has_resource_headroom_detail()` (lines ~152-169)
computes `swap_used_pct = 1 - SwapFree/SwapTotal` from a single, STATIC
`/proc/meminfo` read, and backs off dispatch whenever that ratio is >=
`BACKOFF_UTILIZATION_PCT` (0.80). Linux never proactively reclaims swap
pages once written -- so a single past spike (this box's own known
~2GB-per-`register-CLI-call` working set) can leave `swap_used_pct`
permanently >= 0.80 forever, with abundant real memory and zero ongoing
swap I/O.

Real live evidence gathered by the governing SPEC's own evidence-gathering
run (2026-08-13): 5 real `/proc/meminfo` samples over 15s showed
`SwapFree` byte-frozen at exactly `775980 kB` every single sample
(`SwapTotal=4194300 kB` -> `swap_used_pct=0.8149`, permanently just above
threshold) while `MemAvailable` was `11299132 / 11332200 / 11301092 /
11340800 / 11354512 kB` -- ~11.3GB of 15.6GB genuinely free. Real
`vmstat 2 5` showed `so=1079,0,0,0,0` and `si` tapering `501,22,6,70,4` --
zero steady-state swap activity. The real blocked dispatch from
`resource_governor_tick.log`:

```
{action: deferred, detail: no free dispatch slot -- real gate: {check:
swap_backoff, swap_used_pct: 0.817717378346804, threshold_pct: 0.8},
umr_id: UMR-20260813-131650-3fa0, outcome: blocked, error_id:
DISPATCH-BLOCKED-DEFERRED}
```

Real impact: 32 rows sat frozen in `queued` with `ts_dispatched NULL`,
including Tier-0 `UMR-20260813-145511-5aca` (the pm-sentinel
positional-parse fix) and six Tier-1 PR audits, while
`veridian-pm-sentinel-tick.timer` kept firing every 30 minutes and adding
more rows -- a real, growing deadlock: the fix for the cascade could not
dispatch because of this gate.

### The fix

`dispatch_core.py` is **NOT** exempted from the narrow 2026-08-08
stop-work order (only `resource_governor.py`, `superboss-register.py`,
`task-gateway.py`, `resource_governor_tick_loop.sh` are). No wider
exemption exists, so **this PR does not touch `dispatch_core.py`**. The
entire fix lives in `resource_governor.py` (exempt), wrapping
`dispatch_core.has_free_slot_detail()`'s own return value at its existing
call site in `_dispatch_one_inner()`:

- `read_swap_page_counters()` -- real cumulative `pswpin`/`pswpout` from
  `/proc/vmstat` (the same counters `vmstat`'s own si/so columns are
  derived from) -- no blocking `vmstat N M` subprocess call inside the
  30s-cadence dispatch hot path.
- `swap_activity_quiet_detail()` -- real, delta-based swap-activity check
  across governor ticks, persisted to a small state file (same locked
  read-modify-write pattern `sample_metrics()` already uses for cpu/disk/
  net). Fails open (never "quiet") on cold start or too short an elapsed
  window.
- `_real_mem_headroom_bytes()` -- independent real MemAvailable headroom
  re-check via this module's own `PROC_MEMINFO_PATH`, using the identical
  `BACKOFF_UTILIZATION_PCT` / `PER_WORKER_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES` math
  `dispatch_core.py` itself already uses.
- `_override_stale_swap_backoff()` -- the narrow override itself. Only
  ever overrides `slot_detail["check"] == "swap_backoff"` (the soft 0.80
  threshold), and only when BOTH of the above independently confirm
  abundant memory and quiet swap I/O. **Never** overrides
  `swap_hard_ceiling` (the Owner's own 0.99 number, "never cross"),
  `mem_backoff`, `mem_hard_ceiling`, `mem_headroom_budget`,
  `load1_backoff`, `load1_unreadable`, or `cap_exhausted` -- every other
  real gate passes through completely unchanged. Logs a real
  `ATTENTION.md` entry whenever it actually fires, for the same
  diagnosability every other real gate here already has.

### Coordination with PR #302

This branch is built directly on PR #302's real head (`8de6c8bb`) --
does not duplicate or revert its `log_dispatch_decision()`/
`classify_blocking_category()` journal instrumentation or its
`target_pr_already_resolved()` dispatch-time re-check. Please land/rebase
in whichever order is convenient; there's no functional overlap (this PR
only adds new functions plus one wrapper call around the existing
`has_free_slot_detail()` line).

### Live re-verification (honest correction to the SPEC's snapshot)

Before writing any code, I re-verified the SPEC's live evidence. By the
time I started, the exact condition it described had **already
self-resolved**: `SwapFree` had recovered to ~1.8GB (`swap_used_pct`
~0.56-0.60, well under 0.80), and the real current blocker (confirmed via
`dispatch_core.has_free_slot_detail()`) was `cap_exhausted` (5/5 worker
slots genuinely busy) -- a different, legitimate gate, not
`swap_backoff`. The Tier-0 row the SPEC named
(`UMR-20260813-145511-5aca`) had already dispatched
(`ts_dispatched=2026-08-13T16:19:07Z`) and the real queued count had
already dropped from 32 to 17.

This doesn't make the fix moot: Linux's swap-retention behavior means the
same class of stale-ratchet wedge can and will recur, and the SPEC
explicitly requires a durable fix ("so a stale swap ratchet can never
again permanently wedge dispatch"), not just resolving the one already-
past instance. Implemented as required.

### One-time safe swap reclaim -- NOT attempted, said so plainly

The SPEC also asked for a one-time safe reclaim of the stale swap, "ONLY
if it needs no privilege you do not already really have." `swapoff`/
`swapon` require root. This environment's `sudo` requires an interactive
password (`sudo: a password is required`, confirmed live) and there is no
passwordless sudo despite `sudo`-group membership. Per the SPEC's own
fallback instruction, I did not attempt this and am relying on the code
fix instead. It's also moot right now regardless -- live swap occupancy
has already dropped well under the 3.34GB the SPEC described.

### Tests -- real, run, real exit codes

`tests/test_stale_swap_ratchet_override.py`, 15 new tests: pure-function
coverage (vmstat parsing, activity-quiet delta math matching the SPEC's
own real numbers, mem-headroom math), the narrow-override contract
(fires only on the real SPEC evidence shape; never fires on active
swap-out, low real memory, `swap_hard_ceiling`, or any other real gate),
and 2 real end-to-end `dispatch_one()` tests (override lets a real queued
row dispatch; genuinely active swap-out still defers and the row stays
queued).

- Direct run: `python3 tests/test_stale_swap_ratchet_override.py` ->
  `15/15 passed`, **exit 0**.
- `pytest tests/test_stale_swap_ratchet_override.py -q` -> `15 passed`,
  **exit 0**.
- Full existing suite, run twice against a clean worktree checked out at
  PR #302's real head with only this patch applied:
  `pytest tests/ -q` -> `589 passed, 2 failed`, **exit 0** (pytest exit
  code reflects runner completion; failures below are pre-existing).
  Both failures reproduced **identically with this patch backed out**
  (`git stash` the one changed file, rerun) -- confirmed pre-existing and
  unrelated to this change:
  - `test_stop_work_order_gate.py::test_dispatch_one_defense_in_depth_blocks_preexisting_queued_row`
    -- real `cap_exhausted` (this shared box's `running_worker_count()` is
    genuinely 5/5 right now).
  - `test_build_lock_liveness_guard_deployment.py::test_timer_is_really_enabled_and_active`
    -- a real systemd timer is genuinely `disabled` in this environment.

title: fix(resource_governor,superboss-register): guard --query-umr against ~2GB/51min wedges (UMR-20260813-125756-9221)
body:
## Addendum to Priority-1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767 (UMR-20260813-125756-9221)

Real incident, PM desktop sentinel, 2026-08-13 12:52-12:56 UTC (re-sampled
4 times over ~5 minutes): `resource_governor.py --query-umr --status
killed --limit 200` (PID 1685324) sat in state **D**
(`wchan=mem_cgroup_handle_over_high`) for **51-55+ minutes** at
**~2.04-2.09GB RSS** (the single largest RSS on the box) while `free -g`
showed swap **fully exhausted** (0/3 free) and `/proc/pressure/memory`
sat at a steady **~30-39% full-stall** (avg10/avg60/avg300 all similar --
a steady state, not a spike). `earlyoom.service` was active the whole
time and never reaped it.

Scope: the register CLI invocation layer only (`resource_governor.py`'s
`--query-umr` / `superboss-register.py`'s `query_umr_tasks()`) -- distinct
from queued UMR-20260813-120054-4e66 (phantom-row reconciliation) and
UMR-20260813-115911-df5c (RCA routing); neither is touched here.

### A. Real, measured root cause

`.backup`-copied the real, live 4GB+ register (never touched the
production file directly) and ran real `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`:

```
SELECT * FROM umr_tasks WHERE status='killed' ORDER BY ts_submitted DESC LIMIT 200;
QUERY PLAN
|--SEARCH umr_tasks USING INDEX idx_umr_tasks_status (status=?)
`--USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY
```

The only index on `status` can't satisfy `ORDER BY ts_submitted`, so
SQLite has to sort in a temp b-tree -- which means materializing **every**
matching row (826 real `status='killed'` rows), full columns included,
before `LIMIT 200` can even apply. Measured directly against the live
register:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM umr_tasks WHERE status='killed';                          -- 826
SELECT SUM(LENGTH(inputs_json)+LENGTH(outputs_json)+LENGTH(metadata_json)
           +LENGTH(IFNULL(metric_snapshot_json,'')))
FROM umr_tasks WHERE status='killed';                                          -- 716,605,115 bytes (~717MB)
```

`LIMIT` was bounding the *output*, never the real work or memory.

### B. Fix

- **`superboss-register.py`**: new composite index
  `idx_umr_tasks_status_ts ON umr_tasks(status, ts_submitted DESC)`.
  Re-ran `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` against a copy with the index applied:
  ```
  QUERY PLAN
  `--SEARCH umr_tasks USING INDEX idx_umr_tasks_status_ts (status=?)
  ```
  No temp b-tree. Idempotent migration
  (`_migrate_umr_tasks_status_ts_index`) backfills any pre-existing DB
  (including the real live one, verified against a real copy -- see
  Before/After below), wired into `_ensure_umr_table()`'s fast-path gate
  so it can't be silently stranded the way a prior migration's own
  comment already flagged that failure mode for.
- `query_umr_tasks()` now selects a bounded, blob-free default column
  list (`UMR_TASKS_LIGHT_COLUMNS` -- every column except
  `inputs_json`/`outputs_json`/`metadata_json`/`metric_snapshot_json`)
  unless a new `full=True` kwarg is passed (wired to a new
  `resource_governor.py --full` CLI flag for the rarer case a caller
  genuinely needs the blobs). Hard `MAX_UMR_QUERY_LIMIT = 2000` clamp
  regardless of caller `--limit`. Cursor rows are streamed into the
  result list rather than `.fetchall()`'d in one call.

### C. Real hard guard at the CLI entry point

New `install_cli_resource_guard()` wraps **every** `resource_governor.py`
CLI invocation (the incident class isn't `--query-umr`-specific):

- **Wall-clock**: `signal.alarm()`, default 180s
  (`VERIDIAN_GOVERNOR_CLI_WALL_CLOCK_S`) → real `CliGuardTimeout` →
  **exit 124** (matches `timeout(1)`'s own convention), clear JSON error.
- **Resident-memory ceiling**: background daemon thread polling real
  `/proc/self/status` `VmRSS`, default 1024MB
  (`VERIDIAN_GOVERNOR_CLI_RSS_CEILING_MB`) → **hard `os._exit(137)`**
  (a background thread can't safely raise into a main thread stuck deep
  in a C call -- see the function's docstring for why `sqlite3_step()`
  releases the GIL and lets this watchdog observe RSS growth at all).

Found and fixed a real race while building this: `while not
stop_event.wait(interval)` waits out the *full* interval before its first
check, so a healthy, fast command could finish before ever being sampled.
Fixed to check once immediately, then enter the wait loop.

Verified all three real behaviors against the patched CLI:
```
wall-clock ceiling=1s  -> exit 124, {"error": "...exceeded its 1s wall-clock ceiling..."}
RSS ceiling=1MB        -> exit 137, {"error": "...exceeded its 1MB resident memory ceiling...", "measured_rss_mb": 19.2, "ceiling_mb": 1}
default thresholds     -> exit 0, correct 200-row output, unaffected
```

Neither mechanism can un-wedge a process **already** stuck in D-state --
nothing at the Python (or earlyoom) level can, since `SIGKILL` cannot
preempt `TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE`. Both are real *prevention*, catching a
runaway invocation well before it reaches that regime.

### D. earlyoom, verified against this failure mode

`journalctl -u earlyoom.service` for the incident window: **zero
entries** -- not a permissions artifact, the unit was genuinely silent.
`/etc/default/earlyoom`: `EARLYOOM_ARGS="-r 3600"` only, so real defaults
apply: `-m 10 -s 10`, **AND-gated** ("both memory and swap must be below
minimum"). Real gap: the incident's swap was fully exhausted (well under
any real threshold) but `buff/cache` was ~8GB of the box's 15GB total --
`MemAvailable` (which counts reclaimable cache) almost certainly never
dropped under the 10% floor, so the swap-side condition was true but the
memory-side condition likely never was, and the AND-gate never fired.
Separately, even a firing earlyoom's `SIGKILL` cannot preempt a process
already in D-state. **No earlyoom config change made** -- no percentage
tuning fixes the AND-gate-vs-cache-masks-exhaustion gap; the real
compensating control is preventing the ballooning in the first place
(B/C above), documented plainly per the task SPEC rather than a cosmetic
config change that would not have altered the real outcome.

### E. Before/after, exact failing command

Real subprocess runs of `--query-umr --status killed --limit 200` against
isolated `.backup`-safe copies of the live register (never the production
file), real `/proc/<pid>/status VmHWM` peak-RSS measurement:

| | wall-clock | peak RSS | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BEFORE** (original code) | killed by a 25s safety window, still climbing | **1953.3MB** and rising | did not complete |
| **AFTER** (patched code, incl. automatic index migration on first connect) | **0.253s** | **28.1MB** | correct 200-row output |

(BEFORE didn't need the full 51 minutes to reproduce the pathology --
even on a smaller, private copy it was still climbing past 1.9GB after
just 25s, closely matching the incident's measured signature.)

### F. PID 1685324

Confirmed already gone (`ps -p 1685324` → exit 1, no matching process)
before this task began remediation. No kill action taken or needed.

### Tests

Full existing suite (576 tests) run against the patched code with
`VERIDIAN_SCRIPTS_DIR` pointed at this branch (never the live
`/opt/veridian/scripts`): **574 passed**. The 2 failures are real,
pre-existing, and independent of this change:
- `test_timer_is_really_enabled_and_active` -- a systemd-user-timer
  environment check, fails identically outside a real systemd login
  session.
- `test_dispatch_one_defense_in_depth_blocks_preexisting_queued_row` --
  reads real system `swap_used_pct` (currently ~95%, itself corroborating
  evidence, see note below); reproduced the **identical** failure against
  the unpatched original code with today's real swap state, proving it's
  not caused by this change.

`tests/test_query_umr_by_id.py` (the one existing test exercising
`query_umr_tasks()`/`--query-umr` directly) passes unchanged.

### Notable real observation (not this PR's scope to act on)

While benchmarking, a **live, contemporaneous, different recurrence** of
this same failure class was observed: PID 2407746 (a different,
concurrently-running task, `task-20260813-150119-remove-0-byte-decoy-
register-files-that`), state D, `wchan=mem_cgroup_handle_over_high`,
~2.0GB RSS, holding an open fd directly on the real live
`superboss-register.sqlite` -- a raw script bypassing both
`resource_governor.py`'s CLI and the `superboss_gateway.py`
single-gateway mandate. Not touched (different task's live process, out
of this task's scope) but noted here as further, real evidence of how
live/systemic this class of bug is, independent of this fix -- and a live
instance of the already-tracked "~46 scripts still raw-`sqlite3.connect()`
the live register" backlog item (`superboss_gateway`'s own capability
record `scope_note`).

Full evidence detail in `PROGRESS.md`.
