title: feat(resource_governor): real, bounded retention for telemetry tables in superboss-register.sqlite (UMR-20260813-125836-5809)
body:
## Governing chain

Addendum to Priority-1 `UMR-20260806-171945-5767`. Sibling of `UMR-20260813-125756-9221`
(dispatched the same run, guards the CLI query path) — **this PR is data-volume only and
does not touch the CLI query path.**

UMR for this work: `UMR-20260813-125836-5809`.

## Scope A — real per-table byte breakdown (dbstat, read-only URI, python3 sqlite3)

Measured against the live file (4,091,764,736 bytes at task start) with `mode=ro`, never
locking or corrupting the live register. Top consumers:

| table | bytes | % of file |
|---|---|---|
| `umr_tasks` | 2,132,381,696 | 52.1% |
| `pm_report_snapshots` | 1,805,238,272 | 44.1% |
| `wiring_registry` | 31,453,184 | 0.8% |
| `actions` | 28,717,056 | 0.7% |
| `audit_findings` | 18,833,408 | 0.5% |
| everything else (≈200 objects) | ≈75MB combined | ≈1.8% |

## Re-verifying PRIOR KNOWLEDGE against the real 4.07GB file (not assumed)

1. **"pm_report_snapshots ~200MiB/day"** — **CONFIRMED, still holds.** Real per-day
   `report_json` bytes for the last full days: 08-12 = 211.2MB, 08-11 = 211.2MB,
   08-10 = 211.3MB, 08-09 = 246.3MB, 08-08 = 416.1MB. Row reads of this table are bounded
   everywhere in the codebase: `generate_pm_report_v3.py`'s own `TREND_WINDOW_SIZE = 10`
   (`get_recent_snapshots()`) and `pm_cycle_precheck.py`'s `get_prior_snapshot()` both only
   ever do `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT <=10` — never a full scan.
2. **"umr_tasks is effectively byte-static"** — **FALSE at this size.** It is now the
   *single largest table in the file* (52%, larger than pm_report_snapshots). Row count is
   small and stable (8,212 rows), but its `metadata_json` column average size grew from
   ~55KB/row in 2026-07 to ~262KB/row in 2026-08 (max single row: 7.1MB). This is real,
   ongoing growth this task explicitly could not act on (Scope F) — **flagged here for a
   separate follow-up UMR**, not silently ignored.
3. **"VACUUM alone is pointless"** — **CONFIRMED, still holds** (pre-delete): `freelist_count
   / page_count` was 36 / 998,977 ≈ 0.0000 before any real DELETE ran — there was nothing
   for VACUUM to reclaim. This is why the real fix has to be delete-then-vacuum, not
   vacuum-alone.

## Scope B — telemetry vs source-of-truth classification

**Never touched (source of truth / deterministic-pipeline-read):** `umr_tasks`,
`wiring_registry`, `capability_registry`, `ai_agent_registry`, `owner_priority_sequence`,
`owner_priority_override`, `task_claims`, `pm_decisions_pending`, `master_issue_tracker`,
`ocid_canonical_registry`, `knowledge_engine`, and anything status-mutable.

**Real, append-only telemetry (in scope, 17 tables enabled this PR):**
`pm_report_snapshots`, `log_index`, `directive_compliance_runs`,
`ocid_compliance_audit_log`, `ocid_master_standard_audit_log`, `governance_cycle_log`,
`audit_events`, `audit_runs`, `audit_master_reports`, `audit_orchestration_runs`,
`capability_graduation_log`, `execution_log`, `task_audits`, `intent_unmatched_log`,
`learning_reflections`, `route_replay`, `orchestrator_executions`. Each was grep-verified
to have **zero** `FROM <table>` hits in `resource_governor.py` / `dispatch_core.py` /
`dispatch-tick.py` (the deterministic pipeline), and a real timestamp column to key
retention on. `audit_findings` (status-mutable) and `actions`/`work_items`/`instructions`/
`knowledge_engine` (insufficiently verified in the time available) were deliberately
**excluded** — flagged as follow-up candidates, not silently pruned.

## Scope C — retention policy (all inside `resource_governor.py`; see note below on why no new file)

- `TELEMETRY_RETENTION_TABLES`: table → (ts_column, retention_days). Windows are
  deliberately generous (days, not hours) relative to the bounded-lookback reads above.
- `telemetry_retention_plan(conn, ...)`: real, read-only dry run — counts only, zero writes.
- `_telemetry_retention_archive_table()` + `telemetry_retention_execute(conn, ...)`: real
  archive-then-delete. Every row is streamed (cursor iteration, **never `fetchall()`**) to a
  gzip JSONL file, `fsync`ed, atomically `os.replace()`d into place, **then** the matching
  `DELETE` runs and commits. If archiving a table fails, that table's DELETE never runs.
  The streaming design is the direct, evidenced fix for the sibling UMR's own finding: a
  single *bounded* read of this DB needed ~2.09GB RSS and wedged the box in D-state for 55
  minutes under real memory pressure.
- Archive/state paths are derived **per-connection** from the real DB file in use (`PRAGMA
  database_list`), not a fixed global path — see "real bug caught" below.

### Why no new file (`register_retention.py` etc.)

The task's own stop-work note says `superboss-register.py` and `resource_governor.py` are
"explicitly exempted under the narrow 2026-08-08 stop-work order" and instructs "do not
widen that exemption." Read literally, every other file in `/opt/veridian/scripts` is still
under that order. All new logic therefore lives inside `resource_governor.py` — zero new
files.

## Scope E — recurring, deterministic enforcement through the real existing scheduling path

`~/.config/systemd/user/README.md` documents a **closed set of 19** periodic units — adding
a 20th requires an explicit Owner decision, not automatic worker action. So this is wired as
**Step 13 of `_orchestrator_tick_maintenance()`**, the same once-per-tick maintenance
function Step 12 (wal_checkpoint/VACUUM) already lives in, itself already driven by the real
existing `veridian-cron-dispatch-tick.timer → dispatch-tick.py → run_tick()` path. No new
unit, no ad-hoc mechanism. Step 13 self-gates via a real per-DB state file to run at most
once/24h (matches `credit-accountant.py prune --keep-days 30`'s own once-daily cadence
rather than inventing a new one) — a manual `--telemetry-retention [--execute]` CLI pair is
also added for on-demand dry-run/execute, matching the existing
`--reconcile-stale [--execute]` convention.

### Real bug caught and fixed while building this

Initially the archive dir / state-file path were fixed global constants. While testing I
found that `test_resource_governor_owner_priority_advance.py` (pre-existing, unrelated)
calls `run_tick()` against its own temporary `sqlite3.backup()` copy of the live DB — with
a global path, that test's real archive-then-delete correctly stayed scoped to its own
temp copy for the *data*, but still silently wrote into the *real* production lock-state
file and the *real* production archive directory (confirmed live: found a 111MB archive +
a state file in production paths from a test run, cleaned up before the real production
run below). Fixed by deriving both paths from `conn`'s own `PRAGMA database_list` path, so
a test against a copy never touches production paths. Covered by a new regression test.

## Scope D — real dry run, then real prune, before/after evidence

**Dry run** (`python3 resource_governor.py --telemetry-retention`, live register):
`pm_report_snapshots`: 830 rows would be removed · `log_index`: 2,946 · `directive_compliance_runs`: 3,710 · all other 14 configured tables: 0 (nothing yet past their window).

**Real execute** (`--telemetry-retention --execute`, live register): same three tables
archived-then-deleted for real — 830 / 2,946 / 3,710 rows, three real gzip JSONL archive
files written under `/opt/veridian/ai-os/memory/backups/register_retention_archive/`
(111MB / 140KB / 44KB compressed) **before** their matching `DELETE`s ran.

**wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) + VACUUM**, then real before/after:

| | value |
|---|---|
| file size before | 4,093,345,792 bytes |
| file size after | 2,915,844,096 bytes |
| reduction | 1,177,501,696 bytes (**-1.10GB, -28.8%**) |
| `PRAGMA integrity_check` | **ok** |

## Scope F — umr_tasks proof (absolute constraint)

- `umr_tasks` is not, and structurally cannot be, a key of `TELEMETRY_RETENTION_TABLES` —
  no code path added here ever opens a DELETE/UPDATE cursor against it.
- Row count: **8,212 → 8,217** (grew, from real ongoing live dispatch activity during the
  run — not this code).
- Spot-checked 3 pre-existing rows (including the largest, 7.1MB `metadata_json`)
  byte-for-byte intact after the run.

## Tests

`test_resource_governor_telemetry_retention.py` (new, 6 tests, all passing): plan is
read-only, execute archives-then-deletes correctly, archive content matches exactly what
was deleted, idempotent re-run, `umr_tasks` never configured, and a regression test for the
per-connection path-derivation fix above.
`test_resource_governor_owner_priority_advance.py` (pre-existing, unrelated): re-run clean
(2/2) after the fix, confirmed it no longer touches real production paths.

## Follow-ups flagged, not silently absorbed

- `umr_tasks.metadata_json` bloat (55KB→262KB/row average) — needs its own UMR; Scope F
  forbids touching it here.
- `audit_findings`, `actions`, `work_items`, `instructions`, `knowledge_engine` — plausible
  future retention candidates, deliberately excluded pending the same depth of read-path
  verification done here for the 17 tables that are in scope.
- Three ~4GB one-time `pre-fullfile-backup-20260806*` copies sit under
  `/opt/veridian/ai-os/memory/backups/` (~12GB) — out of scope (not the register itself,
  not telemetry-table retention), noted for a possible separate cleanup.

title: feat(pm-sentinel-tick): stop self-amplifying RCA cascade (UMR-20260813-150004, stacked on #297)
body:
GOVERNING CHAIN: addendum to P1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767. ADJACENT BUT
DISTINCT from queued UMR-20260813-115911-df5c (owns routing killed-task
RCA through the code quality-gate auto-fix loop; already merged, see
`veridian-scripts` PR #305). This PR owns RCA *generation* -- the automated
killed-row RCA path itself emitting duplicate and recursive RCA tasks.

**STACKED ON PR #297** (open at the time this PR was written) -- this
branch is created directly from PR #297's own head commit, not `main`, and
merging must happen in that order (#297 first, then this). See "B" below
for exactly why.

Full real evidence + RCA write-up:
`claude-control` PR #161 (`RCA_20260813_stop_the_self_amplifying_rca_cascade.md`).

## Real incident

- `UMR-20260813-091810-5045` ("RCA: UMR-20260813-060311-6eea killed",
  `completed_unmerged` 09:36:42) and `UMR-20260813-124141-7641` (identical
  title, submitted 12:41:41, ~3h15m later) -- an exact duplicate RCA
  dispatched against a target whose real RCA had already finished. Root
  cause (confirmed live): `UMR-20260813-060311-6eea` was never moved off
  `status=killed` even though its RCA genuinely completed, and
  `is_in_flight()` only checks its own per-tick STATE_FILE for a prior
  dispatch still `queued`/`dispatched`/`running` -- once 5045 reached a real
  terminal status, nothing else stopped 6eea's next resurfacing in Check
  2a's killed-row scan from getting a fresh duplicate.
- `UMR-20260813-131646-007b` ("RCA: UMR-20260813-101802-3ad2 killed") where
  `UMR-20260813-101802-3ad2` was itself "RCA: UMR-20260808-110448-b85c
  killed" -- real RCA-of-RCA recursion, no depth limit anywhere.

## What this PR adds

`pm-sentinel-tick.sh`'s `dispatch_gap()`, gated on `target_key` starting
with `rca:` (Checks 1/2a/2b -- Check 3's `prfix:`/`audit:` targets are
untouched, different semantics):

**B -- target-identifier dedup, reused not reimplemented.** PR #297 adds
`extract_target_identifiers()`/`find_target_identifier_duplicate()` in
`superboss-register.py` for a related but different incident (duplicate
dispatches citing the same PR number). Rather than fork a second
implementation while #297 was still open, this PR branches from its exact
head commit and extends those SAME two functions:
- a 4th identifier class, `umr:<UMR-ID>` (none of #297's three original
  classes -- PR#+repo, file path, script name -- ever match a bare UMR id);
- two new, backward-compatible params on `find_target_identifier_duplicate()`:
  `statuses` (#297's own dispatch-owner-task.sh call site keeps its
  original `queued,running`-only default, unaffected; the new RCA guard
  below passes `queued,dispatched,running,completed,completed_unmerged`,
  since 5045's own already-`completed_unmerged` case is exactly the real
  duplicate that needed catching) and `window_hours<=0` meaning no cutoff
  (a killed row can resurface far outside #297's 4h default).

Wired in as a real `check-target-identifier-duplicate` CLI call inside
`dispatch_gap()`.

**C -- recursion/depth guard.** Every RCA prompt now carries a real
`RCA_DEPTH:<n>` marker (`rca_next_depth()`): 1 if the killed row is not
itself an RCA task, or its own carried depth + 1 if it is. `dispatch_gap()`
refuses once depth exceeds `MAX_RCA_DEPTH` (default 3,
`PM_SENTINEL_MAX_RCA_DEPTH` override) and escalates via the SAME
`notify-owner.py` front door `escalate_financial_decision()` already uses
(`escalate_rca_recursion_limit()`) -- a real, human-visible report instead
of another task, per spec.

**D -- reconciliation.** Of the 10 rows submitted 12:40:20-12:41:41, 9 had
already reached a real terminal status on their own by the time this task
ran; the 10th (`UMR-20260813-124141-7641`, the exact duplicate above) was
real, live `status=running` and was deliberately NOT force-closed (real
unfinished work) -- it has since reached `completed_unmerged` on its own.
No forced closures, no mass-delete. See `claude-control` PR #161 for the
full real query evidence.

**E -- proof.** Two new real tests in `test_pm_sentinel_tick.py`:
- `PmSentinelTickRcaTargetDedupTest` -- seeds an isolated DB with the exact
  5045/6eea/7641 shape, captures the real row-id set before/after a real
  `pm-sentinel-tick.sh` run: **zero new rows**.
- `PmSentinelTickRcaRecursionDepthTest` -- depth increments and is carried
  under the limit; refused + escalated at the limit (real notify-owner.py
  call captured).

Both pass. Full pre-existing suite re-run alongside for regressions (see
this PR's own CI / PROGRESS.md on `claude-control` for the pass count).

## Honest scope disclosure

This PR's diff to `pm-sentinel-tick.sh`/`test_pm_sentinel_tick.py` also
includes the pre-existing, real, live-only content of those two files (per
their own header comments: UMR-20260813-092654-326b /
UMR-20260813-105106-e9a7 work, already running live on the box via its
systemd `--user` timer, but never previously committed to git anywhere --
confirmed via `git log -- pm-sentinel-tick.sh` on the live checkout's own
branch, which only has a 31-line stub). This task's own real fix (the two
guards above) had to be built directly on top of the exact logic actually
executing in production, not a stale committed stub -- so landing that
pre-existing live work into version control was unavoidable to do this
correctly. The `superboss-register.py` diff is scoped to ONLY the
target-identifier-dedup extension described above (no unrelated live-only
changes pulled in).

title: fix(quality-gate): skip node/python lint-build-test gates for docs-only diffs
body:
fix(quality-gate): skip node/python lint-build-test gates for docs-only diffs
Root-caused against 3 blocked RCA-for-killed-task documentation tasks
(task-20260813-104656/-105054/-105503, all RCA'ing an already-SIGKILLed
task and landing a PROGRESS.md/RCA.md-only diff). Gate detection was
purely repo-type-based (package.json present -> always run node
lint/build/test), never diff-content-based, so a doc-only change in
this Next.js monorepo still paid the full `next build` -- which
routinely takes 900s+ and times out under host contention (see the
BUILD_LOCK_* comments already in this file). That timeout fed
worker-entrypoint.sh's auto-fix-then-blocked pipeline a "fix the
build" instruction for a change that touched zero build-relevant
files -- nothing for the AI to fix, and credit-accountant.py correctly
refused the spend every time (confirmed live in all 3 tasks'
worker.log), leaving them permanently status=blocked instead of ever
reaching pending_review.
SPEC (addendum to P1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767) asked for a blanket
skip keyed on task title pattern rca--umr-*-killed. Rejected that
approach: a title is caller-supplied free text, not verified content,
and task-20260813-132414's own prior RCA (PR #145 into claude-control)
already found these same 3 tasks had real src/app/api/... code changes
at the time it looked -- a title-based bypass would have let real code
changes skip lint/build going forward. Gate on the actual diff
instead: DOCS_ONLY is true only when zero changed paths (vs the
default branch) have a code-relevant extension, computed fresh on
every quality-gate.sh run regardless of what the task claims about
itself.
Live-verified against all 3 real blocked tasks (dry run: quality-gate.sh
now exits 0 with a docs_only_skip result instead of a build timeout;
live run: resumed all 3 worker units, all 3 reached status=pending_review).
Stacked on #301 (this branch is based on `fix/quality-gate-untracked-task-build-lock-requeue`,
... more PRs

---

## UPDATE (head d5f0427, 2026-08-13): DOCS_ONLY classifier inverted blocklist -> allowlist

Two independent Tier-1 AUDIT:FAIL rounds were posted against this PR:

1. Head b315ae9: caught `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`,
   `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.eslintrc.yml`, and a bare `Dockerfile`
   being wrongly classified `DOCS_ONLY=1` (gates skipped) by the
   code-relevant-extension blocklist. Fixed at head a63def8e; the auditor
   independently re-ran `tests/test_quality_gate_docs_only.py` at a63def8e
   (12 passed, exit 0) and confirmed those 5 cases were genuinely fixed.
2. Head a63def8e: a second, independent audit proved the same bug class
   was still open -- a blocklist can only ever cover extensions someone
   remembered to add. Real temp-git-repo, single-file-diff runs of the
   real bash `quality-gate.sh` proved `setup.cfg`, `tox.ini`, `pytest.ini`,
   `yarn.lock`, `Cargo.lock`, `poetry.lock` were still misclassified
   `DOCS_ONLY=1` at that head.

This update (head `d5f0427ff4fab2ec2e0ec020e0b83b76c5158dd6`) inverts the
check from a blocklist to a small, closed docs-only **allowlist**
(`*.md`, `*.rst`, `docs/**`, `LICENSE[.ext]`, common image extensions).
Anything not matching the allowlist -- including every case from both
audits, plus any future never-before-seen extension -- now fails closed
to code-relevant (gates run), never open to docs-only (gates skipped).

Real command + real exit code:

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_quality_gate_docs_only.py -v
============================== 30 passed in 1.88s ==============================
$ echo $?
0
```

Additionally verified with a standalone script outside the pytest harness
(real upstream git repo + real clone + single-file second commit + real
`bash quality-gate.sh <workspace> <out>` subprocess) for all of:
`setup.cfg`, `tox.ini`, `pytest.ini`, `yarn.lock`, `Cargo.lock`,
`poetry.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `Gemfile.lock`, `go.sum`, `Makefile`,
`.gitlab-ci.yml`, `renovate.json`, `foo.zzz` (all correctly ran gates), and
`README.md`, `docs/whatever.md` (both correctly still skipped gates).
15/15 passed.

Not self-certifying this fix -- requesting a fresh independent Tier-1
AUDIT against `d5f0427ff4fab2ec2e0ec020e0b83b76c5158dd6`.

## Real root cause behind UMR-20260813-115911-df5c's own redispatch loop

This UMR ("stop routing killed-task RCA through code quality-gate auto-fix loop") has now been dispatched **four times** (task-20260813-132414, -135613, -140326, and now a 4th while this PR was being prepared), each time re-investigating and reconfirming the same already-shipped fix (037908b / claude-control PR #145), because the underlying platform bug that keeps *redispatching* this UMR was never itself fixed. This PR fixes that.

### Bug 1: missing `claude-control` repo mapping

`REPO_LOCAL_PATHS` (`reconcile_stale_running_workers.py`) and `DEFAULT_OCID_RESOLVER_REPO_LOCAL_PATHS` (`superboss-register.py`) had no entry for `claude-control` — the governance/meta repo these very RCA/routing-fix tasks are dispatched against (task.yaml `repo: claude-control`). Without a resolvable `repo_root`, `_real_branch_tip_sha()` / `_first_recent_commit_sha()` could never produce a completion candidate for a claude-control-repo task, so STEP 3's stale-worker reconciliation sweep always fell through to "genuinely ambiguous — real re-queue", no matter how much real, mergeable work the task had actually done. `/opt/veridian/repos/claude-control` is a real, already-existing local checkout — it was just never wired into either dict.

### Bug 2: race between worker handoff and supervisor review

Confirmed live via task-20260813-135613's own checkpoint history: STEP 3's sweep can fire in the real window between `worker-entrypoint.sh` disabling `veridian-worker@<task_id>.service` (the expected, correct handoff the moment a task reaches `pending_review`) and `veridian-supervisor@<task_id>.service` finishing its real review. `ActiveState=inactive` on the WORKER unit alone is not evidence of a crash when the SUPERVISOR unit is still live. This race is what produced task-20260813-140326: the sweep saw `status=pending_review`, no repo mapping (bug 1) → no completion candidate, and requeued a task whose real review (PR #147, correctly rejected as a stale duplicate) was seconds from writing its own real `blocked` checkpoint.

### Fix

Additive only — no existing repo mapping, argparse choice, or decision path changed for any other repo/status combination:
- Add `"claude-control": "/opt/veridian/repos/claude-control"` to both dicts, and to `MARK_TERMINAL_REPO_CHOICES`.
- When `task.yaml` status is `pending_review`, check the paired supervisor unit's `ActiveState` first; skip (`not_settled`) if it's still live/transitional, same shape as the existing worker-unit liveness check.

### Verification
- `python3 -m py_compile` on both files.
- Manually re-ran `_completion_candidates()` / `_real_branch_tip_sha()` against task-20260813-135613's real task.yaml with the fix applied: `claude-control` repo_root now resolves and `git ls-remote` returns the branch's real tip sha (previously always `None`).
- A fresh `reconcile_stale_running_workers.py` dry run against the live DB still exits 0 with no new errors.

Also applied directly to the live `/opt/veridian/scripts/{reconcile_stale_running_workers.py,superboss-register.py}` (same precedent as 037908b) so it takes effect immediately without waiting on review.

## Real gap fixed

Addendum to Priority-1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767, sibling of UMR-20260813-120054-4e66. Governing task: UMR-20260813-135626-reconcile-stale-queued-rows-whose-target.

The governing SPEC's own live evidence (PM desktop sentinel, 2026-08-13 ~11:55 UTC) found 3 real queued rows (`ts_dispatched IS NULL`) each naming a real target PR in their own title that GitHub had already resolved before or shortly after the row was even queued:

- `UMR-20260813-111356-3677` ("...existing PR 249..."): `veridian-scripts` PR #249 **MERGED** `2026-08-13T10:39:54Z`, 34 real minutes **before** the row queued at `11:13:56`.
- `UMR-20260813-101609-9a69` ("Resolve PR 135 conflict..."): `claude-control` PR #135 **MERGED** `10:40:46Z` — no conflict was left to resolve.
- `UMR-20260813-111352-6973` ("...audit-approved PR 136"): real, current `DIRTY`/`mergeable=false`, not the queue-time `UNKNOWN` state.

Every existing dispatch-time guard in `resource_governor.py`'s `_dispatch_one_inner()` (Stage 4/5/6 duplicate-PR guard, OCID-evidence supersession, `reuse_verdict_engine`) checks whether **this task_identity** already produced a PR, or whether an OCID named in the title has newer registry evidence — none of them re-check the **live state of the PR the task's own title names as its work target**. This PR closes that specific gap.

## What changed

- `resource_governor.py`: new `target_pr_already_resolved(title, hint_repo=None)`. Reuses the existing `_referenced_pr_number()` extractor (no new parser), asks GitHub for that PR's real current state via `gh pr view`, and self-rejects only on a real, confirmed `MERGED` or `CLOSED` state. An `OPEN` PR — even `DIRTY` (PR #136's real shape) — is deliberately **not** blocked; the right answer there is a fresh rebase+re-audit dispatch, not a self-reject. Same fail-open philosophy/bounded `GH_PR_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` as every other real `gh` call in this module: a GitHub outage or rate-limit degrades to "no guard, dispatch proceeds", never a wedged queue.
- Wired into `_dispatch_one_inner()` right after the stop-work-order gate, before the OCID-evidence/duplicate-PR guards.
- New action `rejected_target_pr_already_resolved` mapped to Rule 2's `"rejected"` outcome in `RULE2_OUTCOME_MAP`.
- `tests/test_target_pr_dispatch_time_recheck.py`: new, 8 tests.

title: fix(dispatch): write the real per-tick dispatch-blocking reason to the systemd journal
body:
## UMR-20260813-120054-4e66 -- restore the stalled dispatch pipeline

Addendum to Priority-1 `UMR-20260806-171945-5767`, completion of the stalled
row `UMR-20260813-100854-e8a1` (status=running in `umr_tasks` but its unit
`veridian-worker@task-20260813-103211-make-the-merged-write-back-reconciler-ac.service`
was NOT active -- verified live).

### What was actually wrong (real investigation, not the assumed unit)

The PM's own evidence-gathering protocol checks `journalctl --user` on
`veridian-cron-dispatch-tick.service` first. That is the **wrong unit** for
this failure mode: `dispatch-tick.py` (that unit's `ExecStart`) only ever
runs supervisor-sweep / `gap_queue.yaml` / module-queue dispatch -- it never
calls `dispatch_one()` and never touches `umr_tasks` queued rows at all.

The real dispatcher of `umr_tasks` queued rows is
`resource_governor.py`'s `dispatch_one()`, driven by the **always-on**
`veridian-governor-tick.service` loop (`resource_governor_tick_loop.sh`,
`--tick` every 30s). That real per-tick decision already carries a detailed
blocking reason (`dispatch_core.has_free_slot_detail()` -- the
`UMR-20260806-101839-688e` fix that first distinguished `cap_exhausted` from
a real resource-headroom veto) -- but it only ever reached a flat file,
`/opt/veridian/ai-os/tasks/resource_governor_tick.log` (178k+ lines),
because `resource_governor_tick_loop.sh` explicitly redirects the tick
subprocess's own stdout/stderr into that file. **Even journalctl on the
correct unit was silent for this.** That's the real blindness this PR
closes -- not a data gap (the data already existed), a visibility gap.

Historical evidence mined from that flat log (`grep -c` over 178k lines):

| real gate | occurrences |
|---|---|
| `swap_backoff` | 1987 |
| `swap_hard_ceiling` | 807 |
| `cap_exhausted` | 1200 |
| `load1_backoff` | 238 |

Swap-related vetoes dominate. Live-confirmed root cause: this box's swap
sits chronically near/at the 80% `BACKOFF_UTILIZATION_PCT` threshold
(measured live: 82.6% used) from steady-state, non-dispatch processes
(nginx, grafana, dockerd, `beam.smp`/elixir, node/next-server, postgrest --
confirmed via real per-process `VmSwap` in `/proc/*/status`, none of them
dispatch workers), not from worker concurrency itself. The PM's own earlier
evidence explicitly ruled out memory PSI/available-memory as the cause --
correctly, since **swap %** is a distinct, real, currently-reproducible gate
that evidence never checked.

### Fix (this PR)

`dispatch_core.classify_blocking_category()` + `dispatch_core.log_dispatch_decision()`:
a real, best-effort, per-tick line written straight to the systemd journal
(`systemd-cat -t veridian-dispatch-decision`) for **every** `dispatch_one()`
outcome -- dispatched or not -- tagged with one of a small, closed,
real vocabulary:

`cap_exhausted` / `resource_headroom_veto` / `resource_threshold_gate` /
`stop_work_gate` / `dedup_rejection` / `dispatched` / `queue_empty` /
`would_dispatch` / `superboss_unavailable` / `other`

Wired into `resource_governor.run_tick()`'s existing `dispatch_one()` loop
(one call per real tick iteration). Fail-open: a missing `systemd-cat`
binary or any other failure is caught, printed to stderr, and never allowed
to break the real dispatch tick it only observes (same convention as the
existing `record_tick()`/`record_dispatch_event()`).

Live-verified against this exact box's own journald during this task's own
run: `journalctl --user -t veridian-dispatch-decision` immediately started
showing real per-tick decisions, including a real, live `swap_backoff`
(82.2%) block on the very next real governor tick after deployment.

### Scope A -- reconciled the phantom `running` rows (real ops action, this run)

Per SPEC: reused the already-merged `reconcile_stale_running_workers.py`
(PR #249) rather than writing a new one. It was **missing from the live
`/opt/veridian/scripts` checkout entirely** (see drift finding below) --
deployed a byte-identical copy from `origin/main`, ran `--execute` for real
against the live DB. Rows corrected:

| umr_id | unit ActiveState | decision |
|---|---|---|
| `UMR-20260813-104321-99ff` | failed | requeued (no verifiable commit evidence) |
| `UMR-20260813-105106-e9a7` | inactive | requeued (no verifiable commit evidence) |
| `UMR-20260813-105702-b694` | inactive | **failed** (task.yaml self-reported `blocked`) |
| `UMR-20260813-105737-dfc4` | inactive | **failed** (task.yaml self-reported `blocked`) |
| `UMR-20260813-115911-df5c` | inactive | requeued (no verifiable commit evidence) |
| `UMR-20260813-120054-4e66` | **active** | correctly skipped (this task's own row) |

`umr_tasks` `status='running'` count: **10 -> 5** (direct read-only SQL
against `superboss-register.sqlite`, before/after).

### Side finding, flagged not silently fixed

Live `/opt/veridian/scripts` is a real git checkout that has **diverged
from `origin/main` in both directions**: 2 local, never-pushed commits on an
old base (this is *why* `reconcile_stale_running_workers.py` was missing
live at all -- everything after that base, including PR #249, never
deployed), plus real live-only uncommitted/untracked files
(`worker-exit-status-bridge.py`, `session_metadata_sync.py`,
`sweep_awaiting_approval.py`, local edits to `pm-sentinel-tick.sh`/
`quality-gate.sh`). `check_live_scripts_drift.py` already exists and
confirms this. Reconciling that full drift is out of this task's own scope
(risks clobbering real, undocumented live-only work) -- flagged here for a
PM decision, not silently resolved. This PR's own two files were deployed
live surgically (targeted edits preserving the live-only
`UMR-20260813-101757-f13c` fix already present in `resource_governor.py`
live but not yet on `origin/main`), not via a wholesale overwrite.

### Proof (item D)

Before this PR's live deployment: `journalctl --user -t
veridian-dispatch-decision` returned nothing (tag didn't exist yet). After:
real entries appear on every real tick, e.g.:

```
Aug 13 13:40:55 VERIDIAN-DEV veridian-dispatch-decision[2044140]: {"blocking_category": "resource_headroom_veto", "action": "deferred", "umr_id": "UMR-20260813-104321-99ff", "detail": "no free dispatch slot -- real gate: {'check': 'swap_backoff', 'swap_used_pct': 0.821962186777293, 'threshold_pct': 0.8}", ...}
```

`umr_tasks` queued rows genuinely reaching `ts_dispatched IS NOT NULL`
during this task's own run (real, live, not simulated): this task's own row
(`UMR-20260813-120054-4e66`) and 5 others dispatched between 12:39-13:24 UTC
today, confirmed via direct SQL against the live DB.

### Tests

`tests/test_dispatch_decision_journal_logging.py` -- 11 new tests:
exhaustive `classify_blocking_category()` coverage (including the exact
`cap_exhausted` vs `resource_headroom_veto` ambiguity this closes), fail-open
`systemd-cat` behavior, and real `run_tick()` per-tick wiring.

### Full real test suite

```
1170 passed, 14 failed in 369.33s (0:06:09)
```

All 14 failures are **pre-existing and unrelated** to this diff (confirmed:
none of the 14 are in a file this PR touches; `test_stop_work_order_gate.py::
test_dispatch_one_defense_in_depth_blocks_preexisting_queued_row` fails due
to real, live swap pressure (82.6%) tripping the resource-headroom veto
before the stop-work gate runs -- `dispatch_one()`'s own gating order is
unmodified by this PR; this is independent, live confirmation of the same
swap root cause documented above, not a regression):

- `test_deploy_live_scripts.py` (5) -- unrelated, deploy-mechanism tests
- `test_owner_priority_sequence.py` (5) -- unrelated, owner-priority-phase tests
- `test_triage_owner_umr_24h.py` (2) -- unrelated, triage tests
- `tests/test_build_lock_liveness_guard_deployment.py` (1) -- unrelated, real-timer-state test
- `tests/test_stop_work_order_gate.py` (1) -- pre-existing, real-host-swap-pressure flake (see above)

title: fix(quality-gate): don't fake a build-gate failure when a task has no umr_tasks row to requeue
body:
## Root cause

3 RCA-for-killed-task resumption tasks (task-20260813-104656-rca--umr-20260808-183732-d3a3-killed, task-20260813-105054-rca--umr-20260808-175055-cebd-killed, task-20260813-105503-rca--umr-20260808-150937-43d0-killed) were stuck `blocked`, all with the identical `quality-gate-0.json` shape: lint passed, build failed with `output_tail: "build lock contended and the requeue-build-lock-contended CLI call itself failed"`.

Confirmed live via the `superboss_gateway` `/read` endpoint: **zero** `umr_tasks` rows exist for any of these 3 `task_identity` values. These tasks were created directly (task.yaml + systemd unit) rather than through `resource_governor.submit()`, so they were never inserted into `umr_tasks`.

`quality-gate.sh`'s build step, on losing the short build-lock wait, calls `requeue-build-lock-contended` to hand the slot back to the real dispatcher. That command correctly refuses (its lookup helper locates no row to requeue) -- but `quality-gate.sh` then recorded a **fake** `build` gate failure for that refusal, which fed `worker-entrypoint.sh`'s auto-fix loop a nonexistent code defect. `credit-accountant.py` correctly declined to spend on "fixing" code that was never broken, so all 3 tasks stayed wrongly blocked.

## Why not "skip quality gates for RCA-titled tasks" instead

That was the originally proposed fix. Rejected: all 3 tasks' workspaces are real `compliance-tracker` checkouts with genuine source changes (3 merged PRs touching `src/app/api/...`, `src/lib/...`, etc.) -- lint/build legitimately apply to them and passed cleanly except for this one infra gap. A blanket title-pattern exemption would let real code changes bypass lint/build checks for this task class going forward, which is a materially bigger and unrelated risk than the actual, narrow bug located here.

## Fix

When `requeue-build-lock-contended` fails specifically with `"no active (queued/dispatched/running) umr_tasks row found"`, wait out the lock in-process for the existing long-wait duration (same shape as the `loss_count>=4` starvation guard already in this file) instead of fabricating a gate result. Any other requeue failure (DB unreachable, gateway down, etc.) still falls through to the original fake-gate-failure path, preserving that defense-in-depth signal for genuinely unexpected errors.

`bash -n quality-gate.sh` passes. No existing automated test suite covers this file in this repo.

title: fix(systemd): wrap veridian-worker@.service ExecStopPost so a failing post-stop hook can never re-run completed work
body:
## Real, live, fleet-wide defect

Confirmed by the PM desktop sentinel at 2026-08-13T10:55Z on VERIDIAN-DEV. Addendum to
UMR-20260806-171945-5767 (PR #249). Governing task: task-20260813-131054-stop-fleet-wide-worker-crash-loop--missi
(UMR-20260813-105702-b694).

PR #249 merged `worker-exit-status-bridge.py` and wired it in as
`ExecStopPost=/opt/veridian/scripts/worker-exit-status-bridge.py %i`, but the merged
file was never deployed to the live tree. Every stop of every worker unit hit
`Control process exited, code=exited, status=203/EXEC`. Because
`systemd`'s `Restart=on-failure` decision is driven by the unit's overall Result — which
a failing **control process** sets to `exit-code` regardless of the main process's own
exit code — workers that had already finished were restarted from `ExecStart`,
re-running already-completed work, up to `StartLimitBurst=3` times, then permanently
failing. This is the mechanical cause of the duplicate audits/PR comments/branches
this system has been producing.

Live evidence (see this task's own `PROGRESS.md` for full journalctl output):
- task-20260813-104547: 203/EXEC → restart at 10:45:50 / 10:53:45 / 10:55:11, then
  "Start request repeated too quickly" at 10:56:20.
- task-20260813-123933: same loop live at 12:39:37 / 13:07:35 / 13:08:57 / 13:10:13 —
  caught mid-loop at this fix's own start time.
- `systemctl --user list-units 'veridian-worker@*'` showed units in `failed` and
  `activating auto-restart` at time of investigation — steady state, not transient.

## Fix

`systemd/veridian-worker@.service`: wrap `ExecStopPost` in a shell that unconditionally
`exit 0`s:

```
ExecStopPost=/bin/sh -c '/opt/veridian/scripts/worker-exit-status-bridge.py "$1"; ec=$?; if [ "$ec" -ne 0 ]; then echo "[ExecStopPost wrapper] worker-exit-status-bridge.py exited $ec for task $1 -- swallowed so a post-stop hook failure can never re-run completed work via Restart=on-failure" >&2; fi; exit 0' _ %i
```

**Why this mechanism and not `RestartPreventExitStatus=`/`SuccessExitStatus=`:** both of
those only classify `ExecMainStatus` (the main process's own exit code) and have no
effect on a failing *control* process. The actual failure here is in `ExecStopPost`, not
`ExecStart`, so neither option addresses the real trigger. A wrapper that
unconditionally exits 0 is the minimal real mechanism that structurally guarantees an
`ExecStopPost` failure of any kind — missing file, bad permissions, broken interpreter,
syntax error — can never again flip this unit's `Result` and fire `Restart=on-failure`
against already-completed work. Failure visibility is preserved: stderr is still
captured by the unit's existing `StandardError=append:.../systemd.log`, and the wrapped
script's own internal logging (`worker.log`) still runs whenever the process manages to
start at all.

**Scope:** `veridian-worker@.service` only, per the governing task's explicit narrow
scope. `veridian-supervisor@.service` has the identical `ExecStopPost=...%i supervisor`
wiring and the same structural risk (see `worker-exit-status-bridge.py`'s own
"Supervisor-side reuse" docstring) — intentionally **not** touched here; flagging for a
future addendum.

The separately-scoped deployment gap (missing `worker-exit-status-bridge.py` on the live
tree) was closed directly on the live host (file write + sha256 verification against
this repo's `origin/main` blob, mode 0755) as a prerequisite for reproducing/proving this
fix — the *general* merged-to-live deploy automation gap remains explicitly out of scope
here (owned by UMR-20260813-101142-5d24).

## Test plan

New: `tests/test_worker_unit_execstoppost_never_fails.py`
1. `test_unit_file_execstoppost_is_wrapped_to_always_exit_0` — static parse of the real
   unit file, asserts the `ExecStopPost` line is structurally the always-exit-0 wrapper.
2. `test_real_systemd_stop_with_missing_target_does_not_fail_unit_or_restart` — real,
   private, throwaway `systemctl --user` unit whose `ExecStopPost` is the **real** wrapper
   line lifted mechanically from the real unit file, pointed at a deliberately
   nonexistent script (genuinely reproduces 203/EXEC through the real fixed wrapper).
   Asserts `Result=success`, `ActiveState=inactive`/`SubState=dead`, `NRestarts=0`, and
   that `journalctl` shows neither `203/EXEC` nor a scheduled restart.

Verified locally that test 2 genuinely **fails** against the pre-fix unit file — observed
live: `Result=exit-code, NRestarts=3, ActiveState=activating/auto-restart`, i.e. the exact
fleet-wide symptom reproduced through the test harness itself — and passes cleanly
against the fix. Not vacuous.

Ran full existing suite filtered to worker/systemd/unit-related tests
(`pytest tests/ -k "worker or systemd or unit"`, excluding the two files above which are
run separately due to real systemd side effects): **18 passed**.
`tests/test_worker_exit_status_bridge.py` (pre-existing, unaffected by this change): **16
passed**.

Post-merge, this branch's fix (plus the already-deployed bridge script) will need to be
synced to the live unit file at `~/.config/systemd/user/veridian-worker@.service` +
`systemctl --user daemon-reload` for the live effect to persist — done manually as part
of this task's own end-to-end proof (see PROGRESS.md), since the general merged-to-live
deploy automation is out of scope here.
